home_insider.take: Cher, let me tell you about this defense. This is the longest series LSU plays, 117 games since 1896, and we lead it 76-38-3. That's a lot of Saturdays sending cowbells home quiet. Blake Baker's four-man front wants that freshman hearing footsteps, and Charlie Weis Jr. runs Kiffin's veer-and-shoot so Leavitt can push it deep to Watkins. Paul Dietzel, Charles McClendon, Saban, Miles, Orgeron: four national titles' worth of coaches who knew how to welcome a visitor. ESPN rates it third in the whole country on efficiency, and on a scale from 'bland' to 'Saturday night in Death Valley,' this one's already simmering at noon. Lane Kiffin's Tigers lost a heartbreaker at Kentucky last Saturday, 35-34 in overtime, and we've been stewing about it ever since. Sam Leavitt has 1,496 yards and 10 touchdowns, Dilin Jones has 482 rushing yards, and Winston Watkins Jr. is the big-play man. Yes, we're thin at linebacker with Whit Weeks and Charles Ross II out. A freshman quarterback in Tiger Stadium, though? That's a whole roux of a defense, cher.

away_insider.take: Ring it if you mean it, folks, because this cowbell has been thinking hard all week. Here's what the purple-and-gold crowd forgets: LSU is our oldest rival, 117 meetings going back to 1896, and yes, they lead it 76-38-3, but cowbells have rung in Baton Rouge before. Jackie Sherrill and Dan Mullen both built winners here, and today Zach Arnett's 3-3-5 has one job: shorten the game, protect the freshman and lean on Evans. Kamario Taylor has been ruled out with that foot injury, which hurts: 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns and only four picks in Jeff Lebby's veer-and-shoot offense. So redshirt freshman Parker "Billy" Puckett gets the keys at Tiger Stadium. Here's the secret: ESPN's efficiency numbers have our offense 16th in the country, and that system was built to be bigger than one guy. Anthony Evans III, 40 catches for 574 yards, is the safety valve. We're 4-1 and fresh off an open week. The cowbell is calm. Mostly calm.

games.story_text:
Two ranked SEC teams, one league race and a lunchtime kickoff in Baton Rouge. No. 16 Mississippi State (4-1, 2-1 SEC) visits No. 22 LSU (4-2, 1-2) at noon on ESPN, and the loser walks away with a conference loss that could end title dreams.

The biggest news sits in the Bulldogs' quarterback room. Kamario Taylor, who has thrown for 1,450 yards and 17 touchdowns, has been ruled out with a foot injury. Redshirt freshman Parker "Billy" Puckett, who has thrown for 89 yards this season, is set to start. Mississippi State insider Wade Pettus swears the cowbell is calm and the system is bigger than one player. LSU insider Celestine "Cece" Thibodeaux just grins and points to a Tiger defense ESPN rates third in the country, asking how a first-time starter handles Death Valley.

LSU has some wounds of its own. Linebackers Whit Weeks and Charles Ross II are out, and the Tigers are still smarting from last Saturday's 35-34 overtime loss at Kentucky. Sam Leavitt (1,496 yards, 10 touchdowns) and running back Dilin Jones lead an offense that should find room. Mississippi State comes in rested after an open week, but the Tigers' pass rush against a freshman is the matchup we can't stop watching.

Our call: LSU 34, Mississippi State 18.
games.why_this_score: Mississippi State is expected to start redshirt freshman Parker "Billy" Puckett in place of Kamario Taylor, and he faces one of the country's best defenses on the road. LSU's missing linebackers and the Bulldogs' extra week of rest keep this from getting completely out of hand, and gusty wind could slow both passing games. The Tigers' defense is the difference.
games.betting_text: With LSU favored by 17.5 and the total set at 55.5 points, we predict Mississippi State 18, LSU 34. LSU wins by 16, but Mississippi State stays inside the 17.5-point spread and covers. Our projected total of 52 points is under the 55.5, so we expect the game to go under.

fanatic_story.headline: A Freshman, a Cowbell and Death Valley
fanatic_story.dek: With Kamario Taylor ruled out, Parker "Billy" Puckett makes his first career start as No. 16 Mississippi State tries to steal one in Baton Rouge
fanatic_story.body:
BATON ROUGE, La. — The oldest series on LSU's schedule gets a brand-new face under center.

No. 16 Mississippi State (4-1, 2-1 SEC) visits No. 22 LSU (4-2, 1-2) at noon ET on ESPN without quarterback Kamario Taylor, who was ruled out on the final SEC availability report. Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns and four interceptions. Redshirt freshman Parker "Billy" Puckett, who has never started a college game, gets the call, with senior transfer AJ Swann also available.

That is a hard first assignment. ESPN's Football Power Index rates the LSU defense third in the country, and Princewill Umanmielen already has eight sacks. Tiger Stadium seats 102,321, and the Tigers are 4-0 there this season.

Puckett will also be without leading rusher Fluff Bothwell (403 yards), who is out. His best friend should be Anthony Evans III, who has 40 catches for 574 yards and five touchdowns. The Bulldogs come in rested after an open week that followed a 56-23 loss to Alabama on Oct. 3.

LSU has its own wounds. Whit Weeks and tight end Trey'Dez Green are out, and the Tigers are still stinging from last Saturday's 35-34 overtime loss at Kentucky, their second road defeat of the year. Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,496 yards and 10 touchdowns, though his eight interceptions give the Bulldogs something to hunt. Dilin Jones has 482 rushing yards, and Winston Watkins Jr. leads the team with 416 receiving yards.

Both teams need this one in a crowded league race. LSU, in Lane Kiffin's first season, cannot afford a third SEC loss before a trip to Auburn. Mississippi State, in Jeff Lebby's third season, hosts Oklahoma next.

The history leans purple and gold. The schools first met in 1896, and LSU leads the 117-game series 76-38-3. LSU's four national championships came in 1958, 2003, 2007 and 2019. Mississippi State's lone SEC title came in 1941.

Weather could matter, too. ESPN's forecast calls for gusts near 27 mph, which could make life harder on both passing games and on a quarterback making his debut.

Our score assumes Puckett starts, because Taylor was ruled out on the final SEC report. With Puckett, we see LSU 34, Mississippi State 18. If Taylor had played, it would look more like LSU 32, Mississippi State 21.

Our call: LSU 34, Mississippi State 18.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: Welcome to The Tailgate, live from the oldest series LSU plays! I've got a cowbell on my left and a Cajun firecracker on my right. Wade, Cece, my standard opener: what's the one thing everyone gets wrong about your team this week? Wade?

tailgate.speaker: Wade Pettus
tailgate.line: *(one slow cowbell ring)* Ring it if you mean it. Folks think we're done because Kamario Taylor is out. He's thrown 17 touchdowns, so yes, it hurts. But Jeff Lebby's offense was built to be bigger than one man. ESPN has it 16th in the country.

tailgate.speaker: Celestine "Cece" Thibodeaux
tailgate.line: Cher, what people get wrong about LSU is the Kentucky game. We lost 35-34 in overtime, and we've been stewing like a pot of gumbo ever since. We're 4-0 in Tiger Stadium. Nobody is stewing at home.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: Okay, be honest with me, Wade. Parker "Billy" Puckett. Redshirt freshman. First career start. In Baton Rouge. How's the cowbell feeling?

tailgate.speaker: Wade Pettus
tailgate.line: Calm. Mostly calm. He's got AJ Swann behind him if needed, and he's got Anthony Evans III, who has 40 catches for 574 yards. I'd tell the kid what I tell my chickens: keep your head down and find the feed. Evans is the feed.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: Cece, sell me on what Puckett is walking into.

tailgate.speaker: Celestine "Cece" Thibodeaux
tailgate.line: I rate every defense on a spice scale, from 'bland' all the way up to 'Saturday night in Death Valley.' This one is at the top. ESPN ranks it third in the nation, and Princewill Umanmielen has eight sacks. A first start against that? That's a whole roux of a defense, cher.

tailgate.speaker: Wade Pettus
tailgate.line: You're comparing a defense to a sauce.

tailgate.speaker: Celestine "Cece" Thibodeaux
tailgate.line: And you're talking to chickens. We all have our process.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: *(laughing)* Receipts, please, Cece. Any holes in that roux?

tailgate.speaker: Celestine "Cece" Thibodeaux
tailgate.line: A couple. Whit Weeks and Trey'Dez Green are out. And Sam Leavitt has 1,496 yards and 10 touchdowns, but he's thrown eight interceptions, so he can be generous. Dilin Jones and Winston Watkins Jr. help make up for it.

tailgate.speaker: Wade Pettus
tailgate.line: Generous is the best quality in a quarterback. Our guys have been resting since the Alabama game, too. Fresh legs.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: History check, because I did my homework. First meeting in 1896. A hundred and seventeen games. LSU leads 76-38-3. Wade, that's a lot of quiet cowbells.

tailgate.speaker: Wade Pettus
tailgate.line: It is. But every one of those 38 wins rang loud. And this week the wind's gusting near 27 miles an hour. Wind doesn't care about history.

tailgate.speaker: Celestine "Cece" Thibodeaux
tailgate.line: Wind doesn't care about four national championships either, sugar, but we still have them: 1958, 2003, 2007 and 2019.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: Quick one, Cece: Lane Kiffin's first season in Baton Rouge. Grade it so far.

tailgate.speaker: Celestine "Cece" Thibodeaux
tailgate.line: Four and two, perfect at home, and two road heartbreaks. Call it a promising first batch, cher.

tailgate.speaker: Wade Pettus
tailgate.line: And Jeff Lebby's in year three with us. Steady hands. Like a good farmer.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: One last word each. No scores from me, I don't make predictions. Wade?

tailgate.speaker: Wade Pettus
tailgate.line: Keep it close into the fourth, and you'll hear this bell all the way to Starkville. *(ring)*

tailgate.speaker: Celestine "Cece" Thibodeaux
tailgate.line: A freshman, a night-game crowd at noon, and the third-best defense in the country. Pass the hot sauce.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: Cowbells versus crawfish, and I'm full. The magazine's call is LSU 34, Mississippi State 18. For the full preview and every game this week, head to thecoverwindow.com. I'm Roxy Vale. See you at the next tailgate!

home_insider.take: Darling, let's look at the portfolio. Darrell Royal built this place with three national titles from 1963 to 1970, and Mack Brown added 2005, so Florida is walking into a house with four. Earl Campbell and Ricky Williams hang Heismans on these walls. Kyle Flood and AJ Milwee co-run Steve Sarkisian's offense in his sixth season, and Will Muschamp, who coached the Gators from 2011 to 2014, knows Florida football from the inside. Win up front against Baugh and Florida's quarterback has to beat us throwing. Arch Manning, 1,122 yards and 10 touchdowns, is a premium asset. Cam Coleman has five touchdown catches on just 17 grabs, and that's what I call return on investment. And that defense? ESPN ranks it second in the entire country. Now, the Oklahoma loss last Saturday, 27-24 at home? I called an emergency board meeting with myself and we've moved on. Florida brings a quarterback making his first career start and a defense ESPN has 79th. On my balance sheet, that's a distressed asset, y'all. Hook 'em, and kindly mind the brand.

away_insider.take: Observe the Gator in his natural habitat: road games in October, hissing at doubters. Texas wants to talk history? Happy to. This is the program of Steve Spurrier's 1990s teams and Urban Meyer's title teams, with three national championships (1996, 2006, 2008) and three Heisman winners: Spurrier himself, Danny Wuerffel and Tim Tebow. Buster Faulkner's offense wants Baugh downhill early so play-action opens up, and Brad White's multiple-front defense has to keep Manning from hitting Coleman deep. Tramell Jones Jr. makes his first career start today; Pete Thamel at ESPN says Aaron Philo is dressed with that shoulder but only there in an emergency. Philo had been one of the SEC's most efficient passers, with 1,341 yards, nine touchdowns and three interceptions. The sophomore took most of the first-team reps all week. Either way, Jon Sumrall's offense runs through Jadan Baugh, a 12-touchdown bulldozer of a back. ESPN ranks our offense 15th in the nation. Yes, South Carolina bit us last Saturday. Even the apex predator has off days. That play had scales, and this week the scales are on our side.

games.story_text:
Somebody leaves Austin carrying a second straight loss. Texas (4-1, 1-1 SEC) dropped a 27-24 heartbreaker to Oklahoma last Saturday. Florida (4-2, 2-2) fell 38-19 at home to South Carolina the same day. The No. 7 Longhorns host the Gators at noon on ABC with their playoff hopes at stake.

All week the talk has been about Florida's quarterback. Aaron Philo, who has thrown for 1,341 yards with just three interceptions, hurt his shoulder against South Carolina. Tramell Jones Jr. makes his first career start, and Philo is dressed but available only in an emergency. Florida insider Dax Marchetti is narrating the whole thing like a nature special and swears Jadan Baugh, with 672 yards and 12 rushing touchdowns, can carry this offense anyway. Texas insider Caroline "Caro" Whitfield is unbothered. She calls Arch Manning and Cam Coleman "premium assets" and reminds everyone that ESPN ranks the Longhorn defense second in the nation.

Both teams are banged up. Florida is without running back Duke Clark, and receivers Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton are game-time decisions. Texas is missing receiver Kaliq Lockett and lineman Jaydon Chatman. The deciding matchup is Manning against a Gator defense that has struggled, and Baugh against a Longhorn front built to stop him.

With Jones starting, we see it Florida 14, Texas 34. If Philo had been cleared to start, it would look more like Florida 17, Texas 32. Our call rests on Jones starting, with Philo dressed, available only in an emergency.

Our call: Texas 34, Florida 14.
games.why_this_score: Texas has one of the best defenses in the country, and Florida's defense has been leaky, so the Longhorns should control both sides of the ball at home. A first-time starter at quarterback for Florida, along with two receivers who are game-time decisions, makes it harder to keep pace. Both teams had the same rest and the weather looks mild, so the gap in talent and health decides it.
games.betting_text: With Texas favored by 11.5 and the total set at 50.5 points, we predict Florida 14, Texas 34. Texas wins by 20, more than the 11.5-point spread, so Texas covers. Our projected total of 48 points is under the 50.5, so we expect the game to go under.

We project 48 total points, under the posted 50.5.

fanatic_story.headline: A First Start, a Familiar Foe
fanatic_story.dek: Sophomore Tramell Jones Jr. takes over at quarterback as Florida tries to snap a two-game skid against No. 7 Texas and a defensive coordinator who used to run the Gators
fanatic_story.body:
AUSTIN, Texas — Tramell Jones Jr. picked a loud place for his first day at the office.

The Florida sophomore makes his first career start at quarterback today when the Gators (4-2, 2-2 SEC) visit No. 7 Texas (4-1, 1-1) at noon ET on ABC. Aaron Philo hurt his shoulder late in last week's 38-19 home loss to South Carolina and was limited in practice all week. ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Jones took most of the first-team reps, and ESPN says Philo is dressed but available only in an emergency.

Both teams need this one. Florida opened 4-0 and climbed to No. 8 in the AP poll before losing to Missouri and South Carolina. Texas fell 27-24 to Oklahoma last Saturday, and No. 9 Ole Miss visits Austin next week.

Jones brings a small sample. In relief against South Carolina, he completed 6 of 8 passes for 40 yards with an interception and led one late touchdown drive. His best friend today should be Jadan Baugh, who has run for 672 yards and 12 touchdowns. Dallas Wilson leads Florida with 26 catches for 376 yards, and starting receiver Vernell Brown III (knee) is dressed, with his status unclear.

What waits for them is the problem. ESPN's Football Power Index rates the Texas defense second in the nation. Colin Simmons has 9.5 sacks, and the Longhorns allow just 2.81 yards per carry, so every yard Baugh gains will be earned in the trenches.

On the other side, Arch Manning has thrown for 1,122 yards and 10 touchdowns, and Cam Coleman has turned 17 catches into 318 yards and five scores. The same ESPN index ranks Florida's defense 79th.

Then there's the man calling the Texas defense. Will Muschamp, the Longhorns' defensive coordinator, was Florida's head coach from 2011 to 2014.

The series is short but lively. Texas leads 3-1-1, starting with a 7-7 tie in Austin in 1924. After 1940, the schools didn't meet again until 2024, when Texas won 49-17 in Austin. Florida answered 29-21 in Gainesville last October.

The programs own seven national championships between them, and five Heisman Trophy winners: Steve Spurrier, Danny Wuerffel and Tim Tebow for Florida, and Earl Campbell and Ricky Williams for Texas.

Our call rests on Jones starting, which is now confirmed: Texas 34, Florida 14. If Philo had been cleared to start, it would look more like Texas 32, Florida 17.

Our call: Texas 34, Florida 14.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: Welcome to The Tailgate! I've got burnt orange on my left, orange and blue on my right, and I'm the only neutral party in the room, which is how I like it. Dax, Caro, same question I ask everybody: what's the one thing everyone gets wrong about your team this week? Dax, go.

tailgate.speaker: Dax Marchetti
tailgate.line: *(whispering)* Observe the Florida Gator, Roxy. Everyone thinks he's wounded. Two losses, Missouri and South Carolina, and the nature shows say the herd has moved on. But this same animal started 4-0 and climbed to No. 8 in the country. He went into Auburn and won 44-39. He hung 52 on Ole Miss. The apex predator isn't dead. He's... basking.

tailgate.speaker: Caroline "Caro" Whitfield
tailgate.line: Darling, he's basking in a two-game losing streak. What everyone gets wrong about Texas is the Oklahoma game. Yes, we lost 27-24. I called an emergency board meeting with myself, I reviewed the quarterly numbers, and I can report that we are 4-1 with wins over Ohio State and at Tennessee. That's not a down year. That's a correction.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: A correction! Okay, be honest with me, Dax. Your quarterback situation. Aaron Philo is dressed but only available in an emergency, and Tramell Jones Jr. is making his first career start. In Austin. At noon. How are we feeling?

tailgate.speaker: Dax Marchetti
tailgate.line: Here's what I know. Jones replaced Philo in the fourth quarter against South Carolina, went 6 of 8 for 40 yards, and led a touchdown drive. Pete Thamel at ESPN reports he took most of the first-team reps all week. Yes, he threw an interception. Every hatchling bites the wrong thing once. And he won't be alone out there, because the whole offense runs through Jadan Baugh.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: Caro, sell me on what Jones is walking into.

tailgate.speaker: Caroline "Caro" Whitfield
tailgate.line: Gladly. ESPN's Football Power Index has our defense second in the nation. Colin Simmons has 9.5 sacks, and opponents are averaging 2.81 yards a carry against us. In portfolio terms, that defense is our blue-chip stock, the safest money in the building. A young quarterback making his first start against it? That's what we in the business call a high-risk position, sweetheart.

tailgate.speaker: Dax Marchetti
tailgate.line: "High-risk position." She talks like a quarterly report in boots.

tailgate.speaker: Caroline "Caro" Whitfield
tailgate.line: And you talk like a field guide that got wet.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: *(laughing)* Receipts, please, Dax. Why is Baugh the guy?

tailgate.speaker: Dax Marchetti
tailgate.line: Because Baugh has 672 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns, Roxy. Twelve! Observe the running back in his natural habitat: the end zone. ESPN's index ranks our offense 15th in the country. Buster Faulkner wants Baugh running downhill early so the play-action opens up for Dallas Wilson, who leads us with 26 catches for 376 yards. And Vernell Brown III is dressed. If he goes, that's another weapon.

tailgate.speaker: Caroline "Caro" Whitfield
tailgate.line: Cute. Now let's talk about the other side of the ball, where Florida's defense ranks 79th in that same ESPN index. Arch Manning has 1,122 passing yards and 10 touchdowns. Cam Coleman has five touchdown catches on just 17 receptions. Darling, that's a premium asset. That's a touchdown roughly every three and a half catches.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: Okay, now the juicy part. Will Muschamp. Texas's defensive coordinator. Florida's head coach from 2011 to 2014. Dax, does that sting?

tailgate.speaker: Dax Marchetti
tailgate.line: It's like watching a gator you raised from an egg move to a different swamp. He knows our habitat, Roxy. He knows the humidity. He knows where the good mud is. But we've changed a lot since then. New coach in Jon Sumrall, first year. New species entirely.

tailgate.speaker: Caroline "Caro" Whitfield
tailgate.line: We call that an acquisition with insider knowledge, and it's perfectly legal in football. Now he works for a program with four national championships: Darrell Royal's three from 1963 to 1970, and Mack Brown's in 2005. Lovely man. Excellent hire.

tailgate.speaker: Dax Marchetti
tailgate.line: Four titles, sure. We've got three: 1996, 2006 and 2008. Spurrier, then Urban Meyer twice. And three Heisman winners, Spurrier, Wuerffel and Tebow, to your two.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: Ooh. Okay, history check, because I did my homework. This series is 3-1-1 Texas, going back to a 7-7 tie in Austin in 1924. Texas won 49-17 in Austin in 2024. And Dax, I believe your Gators won the last one.

tailgate.speaker: Dax Marchetti
tailgate.line: *(full volume)* TWENTY-NINE to TWENTY-ONE, Roxy! Gainesville, last October! That play had scales! That whole GAME had scales!

tailgate.speaker: Caroline "Caro" Whitfield
tailgate.line: One quarter of a bad investment. It happens. We've rebalanced. And our field is named for Earl Campbell and Ricky Williams. Your boy Jones gets to read their names all afternoon.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: Last word, one sentence each, and no, I'm not asking either of you for a score. I leave predictions to the folks at the magazine. Dax?

tailgate.speaker: Dax Marchetti
tailgate.line: If Baugh gets going early and the kid settles in, Austin's gonna hear a Gator chomp all the way from Gainesville.

tailgate.speaker: Caroline "Caro" Whitfield
tailgate.line: Texas at home, Arch Manning throwing, and a defense ranked second in the nation. Y'all, I'd call that a sound long-term holding. Hook 'em, and kindly mind the brand.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: A nature special versus a shareholders' meeting, and I loved every minute. With Jones starting, the magazine's call is Texas 34, Florida 14. For the full preview, head to thecoverwindow.com. I'm Roxy Vale. Be bold, be kind, and I'll see you at the next tailgate!

home_insider.take: Load up, I don't miss. Pull up a chair: we lead Cincinnati 18-3-1 all-time, and the last time they came calling, in November 2024, we won 31-24. Don Nehlen spent 21 seasons building this place, and Coach Rod, back for his second stint, still calls his own plays out of that option-rooted offense. Zac Alley's multiple 4-2-5 has to keep French from getting comfortable in the pocket. Rich Rodriguez is back on this sideline and the offense has some juice. Michael Hawkins Jr. has 1,055 passing yards with one interception, and Cam Cook is a workhorse with 793 rushing yards and seven touchdowns. DJ Epps averages a mile a catch: 393 yards on 14 grabs. I'll be honest, the secondary is short-handed with safety Da'Mare Williams and nickel Emory Snyder out, and 0-3 in league play hurts. But Milan Puskar Stadium at noon with Country Roads ringing? I've got a pepperoni roll set aside for every Bearcat fumble.

away_insider.take: That's a five-way take, folks: onions, beans, the works. I won't pretend the old Big East days were kind to us here: West Virginia leads this series 18-3-1, and the first meeting in 1921 was a 50-0 loss. That's history, and we're not living in 1921. Luke Fickell's teams taught this program to win big, and Pete Thomas' wide-open offense wants French getting the ball out quick against a Mountaineer secondary missing two starters. Scott Satterfield's Bearcats are 4-1 and coming off an open week, and JC French IV has been tidy, completing 86 of 123 passes for 949 yards and six touchdowns without a pick. Gi'Bran Payne runs hard, and JV Gibson has three touchdown grabs. The Arizona loss on Oct. 4 stung, I won't lie. But ESPN has our offense 44th and theirs on defense 123rd. On the chili scale, that's a matchup with extra cheese. Bring napkins to Morgantown.

games.story_text:
Morgantown at noon can turn a so-so season around, and West Virginia (3-3, 0-3 Big 12) needs that badly. Cincinnati (4-1, 1-1) visits Milan Puskar Stadium on TNT, rested after an open week and looking to stay near the top of the Big 12.

It's a clash of opposite profiles. Cincinnati insider Lionel "Skyline" Abernathy ranks everything in chili ways and calls the Bearcats' tidy passing attack "a five-way take." JC French IV has 949 yards and no interceptions, and ESPN's numbers put the Mountaineers' defense 123rd. West Virginia insider Jolene Buckhannon answers with bravado and a run game. Cam Cook has 793 yards and seven touchdowns, Michael Hawkins Jr. has thrown just one interception, and DJ Epps averages better than 28 yards a catch.

Injuries hit the Mountaineer secondary hardest. Safety Da'Mare Williams and nickel Emory Snyder are out, and cornerback Nick Taylor is questionable, so French should have chances downfield. Cincinnati will be without lineman Aiden Pastoriza and tight end DaMari Witherspoon. West Virginia lost 52-31 to Arizona last Saturday, while Cincinnati hasn't played since a 34-7 loss at Arizona on Oct. 4. Both teams want to wash away a bad memory.

Our call: Cincinnati 34, West Virginia 33.
games.why_this_score: Cincinnati's efficient passing game draws a depleted Mountaineer secondary, and the Bearcats have an extra week of rest. West Virginia's home crowd and Cam Cook's running keep it neck and neck. One late stop should settle it.
games.betting_text: With West Virginia favored by 1.5 and the total set at 63.5 points, we predict Cincinnati 34, West Virginia 33. Cincinnati wins outright as the underdog, so Cincinnati covers the 1.5-point spread. Our projected total of 67 points is over the 63.5, so we expect the game to go over.
games.total_reason_public: The offenses have the edge, led by Cincinnati's attack against the West Virginia defense, and the posted total has climbed from 61.5 to 63.5 since opening. We project 67 total points, over the posted 63.5.

fanatic_story.dek: West Virginia has lost three straight, and a rested Cincinnati passing game is coming to Milan Puskar Stadium
fanatic_story.body:
MORGANTOWN, W.Va. — West Virginia has been scoring. The trouble is everyone else has been scoring more.

The Mountaineers (3-3, 0-3 Big 12) host Cincinnati (4-1, 1-1) at noon ET on TNT, looking to end a three-game slide. They lost 41-24 to Oklahoma State, 45-42 at Iowa State and 52-31 to Arizona. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks the West Virginia defense 123rd in the country.

Cincinnati arrives with fresh legs and a point to prove. The Bearcats had an open week after a 34-7 loss at Arizona on Oct. 4, their only defeat. They are 4-0 at home but 0-1 on the road, so this is a real test of how well Scott Satterfield's fourth team travels.

The man to watch is quarterback JC French IV, who has completed 86 of 123 passes for 949 yards and six touchdowns, with no interceptions on ESPN's stat sheet. Gi'Bran Payne has 392 rushing yards, and JV Gibson has three touchdown catches. The Bearcats' offense ranks 44th in ESPN's efficiency index, which looks a lot better against a defense ranked 123rd.

West Virginia can score with anybody. Rich Rodriguez, in the second season of his second stint, calls his own plays, and Cam Cook is the engine with 153 carries for 793 yards and seven touchdowns. Michael Hawkins Jr. has thrown for 1,055 yards with just one interception, and DJ Epps averages better than 28 yards a catch, 393 yards on 14 receptions.

The Mountaineers' secondary is the worry. Cornerback Nick Taylor is a game-time decision, and several defensive backs are on the injury report. Cincinnati's defense ranks 86th, so Cook and Epps should find room of their own.

History is on West Virginia's side. The Mountaineers lead the series 18-3-1, a run that began with a 50-0 win in 1921. When Cincinnati last visited, in 2024, West Virginia won 31-24.

Don Nehlen spent 21 seasons building Mountaineer football, from 1980 to 2000, and Rodriguez's first run here followed. Cincinnati's modern rise came under Brian Kelly and Luke Fickell.

With rain chances around 34 percent and temperatures in the 40s, ball security could decide a game that looks like it will go to the wire. Cincinnati hosts No. 10 Texas Tech next week. West Virginia heads to TCU.

Our call: Cincinnati 34, West Virginia 33.

home_insider.take: You can't rush a harvest, friends, and Collin Klein's Wildcats have been planting all week. It's the Sunflower Showdown, and Kansas State is 30-6 against Kansas since 1990, and Bill Snyder, the man the stadium's named for, started that run. Now Collin Klein is in his first year as head coach. Sean Gleeson runs the offense, and Jordan Peterson's three-high-safety, odd-stack defense is built to take away the explosive throws Kansas loves. Avery Johnson does it all: 1,092 passing yards, nine touchdowns and another 330 yards on the ground. He's healthy and ready. Jaron Tibbs is the steady target. ESPN ranks our offense 26th, and the Bill Snyder Family Stadium crowd is ready to make some noise after Houston beat us last week. Kansas is in town, and beating Kansas is what I'd call a bumper harvest. Wabash Cannonball at full volume, please.

away_insider.take: I'm only here because of spite and the stats, and the stats say this is the Sunflower Showdown, so spite is fully loaded. It's the Sunflower Showdown, and since 1990 the purple side has won 30 of 36. I know. I can count. But Glen Mason and Mark Mangino both proved Lawrence can win, and Andy Kotelnicki's offense is built on misdirection and motion. D.K. McDonald's 4-2-5 has to keep Johnson from turning broken plays into first downs. Lance Leipold's Jayhawks are 2-3, but Isaiah Marshall averages better than 15 yards a completion: 1,143 yards and eight touchdowns. In hoops terms, that's a lob city. Nik McMillan has 345 receiving yards, Dylan Edwards slashes, and ESPN rates our defense 37th, ahead of theirs. Utah beat us last week. Fine. Manhattan is a shorter drive and a much sweeter rivalry.

games.story_text:

Kansas insider Fitz Calloway claims he showed up purely out of spite. He also loves Isaiah Marshall's deep shots, 1,143 yards at more than 15 yards a completion, along with a Jayhawk defense ESPN rates ahead of K-State's. Kansas State insider Hattie Brandvold, who explains defensive fronts with crop rotation, answers with Avery Johnson. The dual-threat quarterback has 1,092 passing yards and 330 rushing yards, and despite some confusion this week, he is not on the injury report.

The Wildcats' backup quarterback, Blake Barnett, is out, and cornerback Kaleb Patterson is doubtful. Kansas is missing receiver Keaton Kubecka and cornerback Syeed Gibbs, with guard Connor Stroh questionable. K-State lost 35-16 to Houston last Saturday, and Kansas fell 41-24 at Utah the next day. A rivalry crowd should bring out each team's best.

Our call: Kansas State 30, Kansas 26.
games.why_this_score: Avery Johnson's running and passing give Kansas State the most dangerous weapon on the field, and the Wildcats are at home. Kansas has the better defense on paper and can hit big plays, which keeps it close. Neither team is missing a starting quarterback, so this comes down to who controls the ground game.

fanatic_story.headline: Sunflower Showdown, Spring Cleaning Edition
fanatic_story.dek: Both teams are 0-2 in the Big 12, and only one gets to start climbing out today in Manhattan
fanatic_story.body:
MANHATTAN, Kan. — The Sunflower Showdown usually carries bragging rights. This year it also carries a way back into the race.

Kansas (2-3, 0-2 Big 12) visits Kansas State (3-2, 0-2) at noon ET on FS1, and both teams are looking for their first conference win. The Jayhawks lost 41-24 at Utah last Saturday. The Wildcats fell 35-16 at home to Houston.

Kansas State's best answer is quarterback Avery Johnson, who does a little of everything. He has completed 104 of 163 passes for 1,092 yards and nine touchdowns, and he also leads the Wildcats with 330 rushing yards. Jaron Tibbs is his top receiver with 20 catches. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks the K-State offense 26th in the country.

This is a new era in Manhattan. Collin Klein is in his first season as head coach, at a stadium named for Bill Snyder, who led the program from 1989 to 2005 and again from 2009 to 2018.

Kansas, in Lance Leipold's sixth season, throws it down the field. Isaiah Marshall has 1,143 passing yards and eight touchdowns, averaging better than 15 yards a completion. Nik McMillan has 345 receiving yards, and Dylan Edwards adds 318 on the ground. The Jayhawks' defense ranks 37th in ESPN's efficiency index, 30 spots ahead of Kansas State's.

Injuries are close to even. Kansas is without Keaton Kubecka, and Connor Stroh is a game-time decision. Kansas State is missing Kaleb Patterson and Garrett Oakley.

History is the Wildcats' biggest edge. Since 1990, Kansas State has won 30 of the 36 meetings. Kansas fans will point to the Glen Mason and Mark Mangino years as proof that Lawrence can win big, but the recent pages of this rivalry are mostly purple.

The forecast is friendly: 49 degrees and light wind. That should let both offenses play their game, and the team that runs it better probably wins. Kansas hosts Baylor next week. Kansas State goes to Arizona State.

Expect it to stay close. Kansas has the better defense on paper and enough big plays to hang around, but Johnson at home is the most dangerous weapon on the field.

Our call: Kansas State 30, Kansas 26.

Frank Howard coached here for 30 seasons, Danny Ford won the 1981 national title, and Coach Swinney, now in his 19th season, added 2016 and 2018. Chad Morris runs a power-run offense, and Tom Allen's 4-2-5 wants to stop the run and let the pass rush finish. Tait Reynolds has 816 passing yards, Gideon Davidson runs with real purpose with four touchdowns, and Bryant Wesco Jr. is the big-play receiver. Howard's Rock is waiting, and so are all 43 of my orange items. Five-six-seven-SACK, darlin'.

Jamey Chadwell coached here, and this program has three conference titles, the last in 2016. Seth Strickland's offense has to stay patient, and Randall McCray's defense will crowd the box and dare Clemson to throw into the wind. Gabe Giardina's Buccaneers sail into Death Valley at 3-3 after a 49-39 shootout win over South Carolina State last Saturday. Lek Powell's got three passing touchdowns, Hakeem Watters runs hard with six scores, and Mekhi Campfield has four touchdown grabs on 15 catches. An FCS crew boarding an FBS galleon? Mark the logbook. Nobody here is scared of a big ship.

games.story_text:
Howard's Rock, a full stadium and an FCS visitor with a pirate's spirit. Charleston Southern (3-3) comes to Clemson (3-2, 2-1 ACC) at noon on ACC Network looking for the kind of afternoon a small program remembers for decades.

Charleston Southern insider Rafe Guilliard refuses to drop the pirate voice and points to a Buccaneer offense that just scored 49 points in a win over South Carolina State. Hakeem Watters has six rushing touchdowns, and Mekhi Campfield has four touchdown catches. Clemson insider Dixie-Lynn Pruitt, a former Tiger Band flag captain, says the Tigers' open week was all about cleaning up after a 41-13 loss to Miami on Oct. 3.

For Clemson, it's a chance to restore a little rhythm. Tait Reynolds leads the team with 816 passing yards, Gideon Davidson has four rushing touchdowns, and Bryant Wesco Jr. leads the receivers. Christopher Vizzina is still working back from an elbow injury, so the quarterback rotation is worth watching. Wind gusts in the mid-20s could make the passing game choppy, and a bigger, deeper Clemson roster should wear on the Buccaneers as the afternoon goes on.

Our call: Clemson 49, Charleston Southern 8.
games.why_this_score: Clemson has a big talent and depth edge over an FCS opponent, plus two weeks of rest at home. Charleston Southern's offense has scored against FCS teams, but this defense is a big step up. Gusty wind might slow things down a little, though not enough to change the outcome.

fanatic_story.headline: A Little Ship Sails Into Death Valley
fanatic_story.dek: Clemson comes off an open week looking to steady its season, and FCS Charleston Southern gets a shot at a big stage on Military Appreciation Day
fanatic_story.body:
CLEMSON, S.C. — Clemson had two weeks to think about its last game. Charleston Southern gets three hours to change the conversation.

The Tigers (3-2, 2-1 ACC) host the FCS Buccaneers (3-3) at noon ET on ACC Network, on what Clemson is calling Military Appreciation Day. Clemson's last outing was a 41-13 home loss to No. 3 Miami on Oct. 3, followed by an open week to regroup.

This is just the second meeting between the programs. The first came on Sept. 9, 2023, when Clemson won 66-17 at Memorial Stadium.

Clemson's quarterback picture has been foggy. Tait Reynolds leads the team with 816 passing yards on 83-of-128 passing, with one touchdown and three interceptions. Dabo Swinney said this week that Christopher Vizzina, coming back from an elbow injury, still isn't at 100 percent, and reports haven't agreed on who starts. Whoever takes the snaps will lean on Gideon Davidson, who has 371 rushing yards and four touchdowns, and receiver Bryant Wesco Jr., who has 25 catches for 315 yards. Will Heldt leads the defense with four sacks.

Charleston Southern comes in on a high. The Buccaneers beat South Carolina State 49-39 last Saturday. Hakeem Watters has six rushing touchdowns, and Mekhi Campfield has four touchdown catches on just 15 receptions. Lek Powell has thrown for 552 yards. Steve Zayachkowsky does a bit of everything on defense, leading the team in both tackles (57) and sacks (two).

The gap in tradition is wide. Clemson claims national titles from 1981, 2016 and 2018, and Dabo Swinney is in his 19th season. The playing surface is Frank Howard Field, named for the coach who led the Tigers from 1940 to 1969. Charleston Southern, coached by Gabe Giardina, has three Big South titles, the latest in 2016, when Jamey Chadwell was in charge.

The forecast calls for gusts near 24 mph, which could slow the passing games a little.

For Clemson, this is a chance to get its offense right before Virginia Tech visits next week. For Charleston Southern, it's a chance to measure itself against one of the sport's big names.

Our call: Clemson 49, Charleston Southern 8.

home_insider.take: Objection: sustained. Pitt brags about Pop Warner? Fine. We have Frank Leahy's 1940 team and Doug Flutie's 1984 Heisman, and every Eagle knows the pass. Bill O'Brien calls the offense himself this year, and Ted Roof's 4-3 defense ranks 58th to Pitt's 53rd-ranked offense. It's tight, and the wind and McKenzie's legs could tip it. Your Honor, Boston College is 2-3 but rested, coming off an open week, with Bill O'Brien drawing up a plan. Mason McKenzie is our whole case. He has 967 passing yards and leads the team with 437 rushing yards. Pittsburgh is starting a true freshman with no career starts against a defense that's had two weeks to prepare. And the wind forecast at Alumni Stadium is wicked. I rest my case, and I'm appointing myself judge.

away_insider.take: Dat's a yinz problem, not a yikes problem. Pitt has nine claimed national titles, from Pop Warner and Jock Sutherland in the early days to Johnny Majors and Tony Dorsett in 1976. That's not nothing, Boston. Coach Narduzzi is in his 12th season, Cory Sanders' 4-3 defense ranks 30th by ESPN, and Kade Bell's hurry-up offense just needs the kid, Corey Dailey, to protect the football. Losing Mason Heintschel for the season with a torn ACL hurts, n'at. He had 14 touchdowns and one pick. But Pat Narduzzi's defense is the steel here, and ESPN ranks it 30th. Holden Geriner got the first start after that, a 21-17 loss to Carolina, and now true freshman Corey Dailey gets his first career start. Four-star kid, 100 touchdown passes in high school. Cataurus Hicks has 365 receiving yards. We're 5-1. Grade on the whistle: pure steel.

games.story_text:
Pitt (5-1, 2-1 ACC) is learning to win without its quarterback. Mason Heintschel tore his ACL against Virginia Tech, and Holden Geriner made his first career start last Saturday in a 21-17 loss to North Carolina. Now Pitt turns to true freshman Corey Dailey, who has no career starts, as the Panthers head to Chestnut Hill to face Boston College (2-3, 0-2) at noon on ESPN2.

Pittsburgh insider Dominic "Yinz" Bertolucci grades every tackle on a "yinz-to-yikes" scale and says the defense is the steel. ESPN rates it 30th nationally, against a Boston College offense ranked near the bottom of the country. Boston College insider Siobhan Dunleavy argues every play like a moot-court case. Her exhibit is Mason McKenzie, the Eagles' leading passer and leading rusher, plus an open week to prepare for a true freshman making his first career start.

Pitt's final report rules out safety Josh Guerrier, running back Ja'Kyrian Turner and cornerback Rashan Murray, and defensive tackle Nick James is a game-time decision. Boston College is also missing two defensive backs and running back Sedric Addison. The weather could matter most of all, with gusts near 39 mph forecast. That should keep the ball on the ground and favor the steadier defense.

Our call: Pittsburgh 24, Boston College 15.
games.why_this_score: Pitt's defense is much stronger than Boston College's offense, which should make up for a true freshman making his first start at quarterback. Strong wind should limit passing for both teams and turn this into a field-position game. BC's extra rest helps keep it within reach.
games.betting_text: With Pittsburgh favored by 6.5 and the total set at 42.5 points, we predict Pittsburgh 24, Boston College 15. Pittsburgh wins by 9, more than the 6.5-point spread, so Pittsburgh covers. Our projected total of 39 points is under the 42.5, so we expect the game to go under.
games.total_reason_public: The defenses have the edge, especially Pittsburgh's defense against the Boston College offense, the posted total has dropped from 46.5 to 42.5 since opening, Pitt is starting true freshman Corey Dailey (no career starts) after losing Mason Heintschel for the season, and the forecast calls for wind gusts around 39 mph. We project 39 total points, under the posted 42.5.

fanatic_story.headline: A True Freshman Takes the Wheel in the Wind
fanatic_story.dek: With Mason Heintschel lost for the season, Pitt hands its offense to first-time starter Corey Dailey at Boston College
fanatic_story.body:
CHESTNUT HILL, Mass. — Pitt's quarterback depth chart has turned over twice in two weeks.

Mason Heintschel, who threw 14 touchdowns against one interception, is out for the season with a torn ACL. Holden Geriner started last week's 21-17 loss to North Carolina. Now Pitt's official game-day report names true freshman Corey Dailey, who has no career starts, as the starter at Boston College at noon ET on ESPN2.

The Panthers (5-1, 2-1 ACC) still bring the steadier team to Alumni Stadium. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks Pitt's defense 30th in the country, and Boston College's offense ranks 123rd. Cataurus Hicks leads Pitt with 365 receiving yards, so expect Dailey to look his way.

Boston College (2-3, 0-2) is rested after an open week that followed a 25-16 loss at SMU. Bill O'Brien, in his third season, calls the offense himself, and almost everything runs through quarterback Mason McKenzie. He has 967 passing yards and also leads the Eagles with 437 rushing yards. The Eagles are without Cameron Martinez.

Weather could be the biggest story of the day. ESPN's forecast has gusts near 39 mph with a chance of rain, which could keep both teams on the ground and make this a field-position game. That would help no team more than the one with the better defense, and on paper that is Pitt.

The series is close. Pitt leads 19-16 in 35 meetings dating to 1959, according to Pitt's official records. The Panthers won the most recent game 48-7 in Pittsburgh last season, but Boston College won 34-23 the year before in Chestnut Hill.

Both programs have rich pasts. Pitt claims nine national championships, the latest in 1976, the same year Tony Dorsett won the Heisman Trophy. Boston College's Doug Flutie won the Heisman in 1984, and the Eagles claim a 1940 national title under Frank Leahy.

Pat Narduzzi's Panthers head to No. 3 Miami next week, so this is a chance to bank a road win before a hard stretch. Boston College visits Georgia Tech.

Our score was set with Geriner expected to start. With Geriner, we have Pittsburgh 24, Boston College 15. With Dailey now confirmed as the starter, it tightens to Pittsburgh 22, Boston College 17, so the second score is the one to watch.

Our call: Pittsburgh 24, Boston College 15.

Coach Lashlee is in his fifth season, with three co-offensive coordinators, Rob Likens, Garin Justice and D'Eriq King, and a 4-2-5 defense. Jennings against a depleted Cavalier secondary is the outfit of the night. Rhett Lashlee's Mustangs are ranked 24th, 4-1, and rested after an open week. Kevin Jennings has 1,588 yards and 14 touchdowns, Kendrick Raphael has six rushing scores, and Yamir Knight is a speed merchant. Virginia's secondary arrives missing half its starters. That outfit doesn't match, darling. Ford Stadium is going to be fashion week with a scoreboard.

away_insider.take: As Mr. George Welsh spent 19 seasons building Charlottesville into a winner, and that's the blueprint: smart, tough, patient. Desmond Kitchings' offense runs through Pribula. John Rudzinski's multiple 4-2-5 will need every healthy body on the back end against Jennings and the Mustangs. Jefferson would've charted it, a 4-2 start with a 28-25 win over Syracuse is a fine piece of architecture. Beau Pribula is our cornerstone: 13 touchdowns and one interception. Tony Elliott has the Cavaliers playing composed football. I won't pretend the injury list isn't long. Starting cornerback Omillio Agard is out for the season, and safeties Corey Costner and Brandyn Hillman were ruled out too. Even so, Pribula's decision-making travels well, even to Dallas. Wahoowa from the Grounds.

SMU insider Tatum Delacroix-Price, sweet but savage, has already graded Virginia's sideline and found it short-handed. She's not wrong. The Cavaliers' final report lists 24 players out, including season-ending news for starting cornerback Omillio Agard, plus safeties Corey Costner and Brandyn Hillman and linebacker Caleb Hardy.

That puts Kevin Jennings in a great spot. The SMU quarterback has 1,588 yards and 14 touchdowns, and Kendrick Raphael adds six rushing scores. The Mustangs have injuries too, including running backs Dramekco Green and Link Rhodes, receivers Carterrious Brown and Daylon Singleton, and two linebackers. Still, SMU comes in off an open week while Virginia played last Saturday.

Our call: SMU 30, Virginia 21.
games.why_this_score: Virginia's secondary is badly depleted, and that's a tough matchup against Kevin Jennings' passing. SMU also had an open week and plays at home. Pribula's ball security keeps the Cavaliers in it, but it's hard to slow SMU with this many defenders out.

fanatic_story.headline: Pribula's Poise Meets a Pony Express
fanatic_story.dek: No. 24 SMU, rested and unbeaten at home, hosts a Virginia team whose secondary arrives short-handed
fanatic_story.body:
DALLAS — The second meeting in this young series has a clear question at its center: can a depleted Virginia secondary keep up with Kevin Jennings?

No. 24 SMU (4-1, 2-1 ACC) hosts Virginia (4-2, 2-1) at noon ET on CW, coming off an open week. The Mustangs are 3-0 at home. Their only loss came 41-31 at Louisville on Sept. 19.

Jennings has been sharp, completing 117 of 156 passes for 1,588 yards and 14 touchdowns, with five interceptions. Kendrick Raphael has six rushing touchdowns, and Yamir Knight leads the receivers with 29 catches for 367 yards. On defense, Marques White has 4.5 sacks. Rhett Lashlee, in his fifth season, calls the plays himself.

Virginia's defense will be stretched thin. Cornerback Omillio Agard and safety Brandyn Hillman are out, along with several reserves. That is a hard way to face an offense that ranks 37th in ESPN's Football Power Index efficiency ratings.

The Cavaliers' best weapon is ball security. Quarterback Beau Pribula has thrown 13 touchdown passes and just one interception for 1,074 yards. Jekail Middlebrook leads the ground game with 337 yards. Virginia beat Syracuse 28-25 last week to move to 2-1 in league play, but it has struggled away from Charlottesville, losing 38-7 at Florida State on Oct. 3.

Tony Elliott, in his fifth season, has Virginia playing composed football, and its defense, 40th in ESPN's index, is better than its injury report suggests. Still, keeping SMU's passing game in front of a patched-up secondary for four quarters is a tall ask.

The programs have met only once. SMU won 33-7 in Charlottesville on Nov. 23, 2024. They were supposed to meet in the 2021 Fenway Bowl, but that game was canceled.

History is on the hosts' side in other ways, too. SMU's Doak Walker won the Heisman Trophy in 1948, and the Mustangs claim national titles from 1935, 1981 and 1982. Virginia's high-water mark came under George Welsh, who coached from 1982 to 2000, and the Cavaliers won ACC titles in 1989 and 1995.

The weather in Dallas should be ideal at 57 degrees with light wind. Virginia hosts Duke on Oct. 23, and SMU welcomes California next Saturday.

Pribula can keep this close if he keeps protecting the ball. SMU's passing game against a short-handed secondary is the difference.

Our call: SMU 30, Virginia 21.

The trenches may decide it. Ohio State is without starting lineman Austin Siereveld and fellow lineman Jaxon Powell, plus running backs Ja'Kobi Jackson and Anthony Rogers. Bo Jackson, the Buckeyes' leading rusher, carries the load. Indiana's report is much lighter. Both teams won last Saturday: Ohio State beat Maryland 45-16, and Indiana edged Nebraska 20-17 on the road.

Our call: Ohio State 26, Indiana 25.

fanatic_story.headline: The Champs Defend Their House
fanatic_story.dek: Undefeated No. 5 Indiana, the defending national champion, hosts No. 4 Ohio State in a rematch of last season's Big Ten title game
fanatic_story.body:
BLOOMINGTON, Ind. — The last time these teams met, Indiana won a Big Ten championship. This time, the Hoosiers get to defend their title at home.

No. 5 Indiana (6-0, 3-0 Big Ten) hosts No. 4 Ohio State (5-1, 3-0) at noon ET on Fox in a matchup of unbeaten league records. Indiana beat Ohio State 13-10 in the 2025 Big Ten Championship Game in Indianapolis and went on to win the national title. Fernando Mendoza won the Heisman Trophy that season.

It's hard to find a gap between these teams. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks Indiana's offense fourth and its defense 13th, and Ohio State's offense and defense both sixth.

Ohio State's passing game might be the best in the country. Julian Sayin has thrown for 1,772 yards with 17 touchdowns and two interceptions, and Jeremiah Smith has 48 catches for 916 yards and 11 touchdowns. Bo Jackson has 460 rushing yards. The Buckeyes' only loss was 24-23 at Texas on Sept. 12, and they get receivers Brandon Inniss and Devin McCuin back this week. They're without starting front man Austin Siereveld.

Indiana answers with a quarterback who hasn't thrown an interception on ESPN's stat sheet. Josh Hoover has 17 touchdown passes on 88-of-129 passing for 1,364 yards. Turbo Richard averages more than eight yards a carry, 597 yards on 71 attempts, and Charlie Becker has eight touchdown catches. Tobi Osunsanmi leads the defense with five sacks. The Hoosiers survived a 20-17 game at Nebraska last week.

Curt Cignetti, in his third season, is 33-2 at Indiana. Ryan Day, in his eighth season, is 87-13 at Ohio State.

The long view still belongs to Ohio State. The Buckeyes lead the all-time series 81-13-5, according to Indiana's records, and have nine national championships, most recently in 2024, along with seven Heisman Trophies. But last December's result shows how much has changed.

The weather should cooperate at 49 degrees with light wind. The winner takes control of the Big Ten race, and the stakes don't ease up from here: Ohio State goes to No. 19 USC on Oct. 31, and Indiana visits Michigan next week.

Expect a fourth-quarter finish. Indiana has home field and a healthier front, but Smith gives Ohio State the slimmest edge.

Our call: Ohio State 26, Indiana 25.

And the head coach on our sideline today is Pat Fitzgerald, Northwestern's longtime coach, in year one in East Lansing. He knows their playbook. Joe Rossi's multiple 4-2-5 wants pressure on Chiles before he finds Wilde. Strike three. Pat Fitzgerald's Spartans are 2-4 and lost to Illinois 38-37 in overtime last week. That one stung, eh. Alessio Milivojevic has 1,047 yards, and Rodney Bullard Jr. is a tough target. I'll be honest: we're missing four cornerbacks, two linebackers, left tackle Ben Murawski and running back Cam Edwards for the season. But Spartan Stadium never quits, and that marching band could win games on its own.

away_insider.take: Footnote: I was right. Ara Parseghian coached here before Notre Dame, and Gary Barnett and Randy Walker won here too. This is a smart program, and it travels. Chip Kelly coordinates our offense, 10th in ESPN's numbers, and Tim McGarigle's multiple 4-3 has to make up for Fitzgerald's absence. David Braun's Wildcats are ranked 25th, 4-1, and Aidan Chiles hasn't thrown an interception all year: 1,172 yards and nine touchdowns. Griffin Wilde has 425 receiving yards. ESPN ranks our offense 10th. Footnote two: that's really good. We lose safety Robert Fitzgerald, our leading tackler, and tight end Luke Dehnicke, which genuinely hurts. Even so, Michigan State's cornerback room is basically empty, and I've already drafted a strongly worded editorial about throwing it every down.

games.story_text:
A ranked team visits East Lansing, and the Spartans would love to spoil the party. No. 25 Northwestern (4-1, 1-1 Big Ten) visits Michigan State (2-4, 0-3) at noon on Peacock. The Wildcats are trying to stay ranked, while the Spartans need a win to keep bowl hopes alive.

Northwestern insider Ezra Lindqvist footnotes his own jokes, and he can back them up. Aidan Chiles has 1,172 yards and no interceptions, Griffin Wilde has 425 receiving yards, and ESPN ranks the Wildcat offense 10th. Michigan State insider Shay Kowalczyk frames every defensive call like a catcher. She admits the glove is thin this week: cornerbacks Tre Bell, Tyran Chappell, Charles Brantley and Keshawn Williams are all out, along with linebackers Jordan Hall and Brady Pretzlaff and left tackle Ben Murawski. Running back Cam Edwards is out for the season.

Northwestern has losses too. Safety Robert Fitzgerald, its leading tackler, is out, and so is tight end Luke Dehnicke. Michigan State played well in last week's 38-37 overtime loss to Illinois, and Alessio Milivojevic gives the Spartans a puncher's chance.

Our call: Northwestern 30, Michigan State 20.

fanatic_story.headline: Fitzgerald Meets His Old Team
fanatic_story.dek: Pat Fitzgerald coached Northwestern for 17 seasons. Now his short-handed Michigan State team hosts No. 25 Northwestern
fanatic_story.body:
EAST LANSING, Mich. — Pat Fitzgerald knows exactly what is coming through the tunnel. The question is whether his Michigan State roster can do anything about it.

Fitzgerald led Northwestern from 2006 to 2022. Now in his first season at Michigan State, he hosts his old program at noon ET on Peacock. No. 25 Northwestern (4-1, 1-1 Big Ten) brings one of the country's most efficient offenses. Michigan State (2-4, 0-3) has lost four in a row, most recently 38-37 in overtime to Illinois.

The Wildcats' offense, coordinated by Chip Kelly, ranks 10th in ESPN's Football Power Index efficiency ratings. Quarterback Aidan Chiles has completed 80 of 112 passes for 1,172 yards and nine touchdowns, with no interceptions on ESPN's stat sheet. Griffin Wilde leads the receivers with 24 catches for 425 yards, and Caleb Komolafe has 334 rushing yards. Northwestern's only loss came 29-23 at Indiana.

That's a tough matchup for a Michigan State defense that ranks 71st and is badly short-handed. Cornerbacks Tre Bell and Charles Brantley are out, along with defender Brady Pretzlaff, left tackle Ben Murawski and running back Cam Edwards.

Northwestern has an important absence, too. Safety Robert Fitzgerald, the team's leading tackler with 49 stops, is out. That could open things up for Spartans quarterback Alessio Milivojevic, who has 1,047 passing yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions. Rodney Bullard Jr. is his top target.

David Braun, in his fourth season at Northwestern, has the Wildcats ranked for the first time this year. A win would keep them in the Big Ten race before they host Rutgers next week. Michigan State, which visits No. 12 UCLA next, needs a spark.

This is the 61st meeting, and Michigan State leads the series 40-20, according to the school's game notes. The Spartans have won three in a row, most recently 38-21 in Evanston in 2021, when Fitzgerald was on the other side.

Michigan State's history runs deep, with national championships under Biggie Munn and Duffy Daugherty between 1951 and 1966. Northwestern's proudest modern stretch came in the 1990s, with Big Ten titles in 1995, 1996 and 2000.

Calm weather, 48 degrees and little wind, should suit the better passing team. On paper, that's Northwestern.

Our call: Northwestern 30, Michigan State 20.

fanatic_story.headline: The Air Raid Meets the Wind at West Point
fanatic_story.dek: Florida Atlantic's precise passing game visits Army on a gusty day that could suit the Black Knights' triple option
fanatic_story.body:
WEST POINT, N.Y. — Florida Atlantic wants to throw. The weather at Michie Stadium may have other plans.

The Owls (4-1, 1-0 American) visit Army (3-2, 2-1) at noon ET on CBS Sports Network, and ESPN's forecast calls for gusts near 37 mph with a chance of rain. That is welcome news for an Army offense built on the triple option, which keeps the ball on the ground and the clock moving.

Army's engine is quarterback Cale Hellums, who leads the team with 104 carries for 524 yards and eight touchdowns and has thrown for 356 more. The Black Knights beat Tulane 20-17 last Saturday. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks Army's offense 27th in efficiency.

Florida Atlantic's offense is built on precision. Caden Veltkamp has completed 128 of 175 passes for 1,427 yards, 12 touchdowns and two interceptions. Kelby Valsin is his top target with 40 catches for 512 yards and five scores. The Owls have had two weeks to prepare since a 66-10 win over Texas Southern on Oct. 3, and their only loss came at Florida in the season opener.

Both defenses have struggled. ESPN's index ranks FAU's defense 112th and Army's 129th. That suggests whoever controls the clock controls the afternoon, which is what Army's option is designed to do. Facing the triple option means every defender has to handle his own assignment on every snap, and one missed read can turn into a long run.

The teams have met once. Army won 24-7 in Boca Raton on Sept. 7, 2024.

The two programs could hardly be more different in age. Florida Atlantic played its first season in 2001 under Howard Schnellenberger. Army has been playing since 1890, claims national titles from 1914, 1916 and 1944 through 1946, and counts three Heisman Trophy winners: Doc Blanchard in 1945, Glenn Davis in 1946 and Pete Dawkins in 1958. Jeff Monken has led the Black Knights since 2014.

Neither team listed a notable injury, so this should come down to style. FAU hosts Rice next week, while Army plays at Tulsa on Oct. 23.

Veltkamp's accuracy and FAU's extra rest should keep it close. In this wind, Army's ground game should be enough.

Our call: Army 31, Florida Atlantic 27.

fanatic_story.headline: Bowling Green Chases a 3-0 MAC Start
fanatic_story.dek: The Falcons are unbeaten in league play, and a struggling Ball State team visits Doyt Perry Stadium looking for a turnaround
fanatic_story.body:
BOWLING GREEN, Ohio — Bowling Green's season has turned in two weeks. Ball State is still waiting for its turn.

The Falcons (2-4, 2-0 MAC) host Ball State (1-5, 0-2) at noon ET on ESPN+, looking to stay perfect in league play. After three losses to start the year, including at Nebraska and Iowa State, Bowling Green won 24-20 at Miami (Ohio) and beat Sacramento State 38-10 last week.

Eddie George, in his second season as Bowling Green's coach, has built a team that wins with defense and grit. Myles Bradley has seven sacks, and Dorian Pringle has 56 tackles. Quarterback Jay Kastantin has thrown for 986 yards, Austyn Dendy leads the ground game, and Jeremiah Scoby has 24 catches.

Ball State is searching. The Cardinals are 0-4 on the road and coming off a 45-14 loss at No. 25 Northwestern. Quarterback Keldric Luster, back after missing time in September with a foot injury, has 871 passing yards with six touchdowns. TJ Horton has five rushing touchdowns, and Donovan Hamilton is the top receiver with 22 catches.

Points could be scarce. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks Bowling Green's offense 134th in efficiency and Ball State's 102nd. On the other side, Ball State's defense ranks 134th and Bowling Green's 94th. In a game between two offenses that have struggled, one big play could be the difference, and Horton has shown he can break one.

Bowling Green has owned this series lately. The Falcons lead it 23-9-1 and have won the past three meetings, according to Ball State's game notes.

The Falcons' history includes coaching names that went on to bigger things: Doyt Perry, whose name is on the stadium, Don Nehlen and Urban Meyer. Bowling Green has won 17 conference titles. Ball State has 11, the most recent a MAC title in 2020.

The weather should be crisp, at 47 degrees with light wind, and neither team listed injuries of note.

A win would set up Bowling Green nicely for a trip to Buffalo next week. Ball State returns home to face Sacramento State.

Bowling Green's defense and home crowd give it the edge, but Ball State's ground game should keep it close.

Our call: Bowling Green 27, Ball State 20.

fanatic_story.headline: Perfect Dukes, Rested Panthers
fanatic_story.dek: Unbeaten James Madison brings its 6-0 start and a five-game series streak into a home date with a Georgia State team coming off two weeks of rest
fanatic_story.body:
HARRISONBURG, Va. — James Madison has not lost yet this season, and it has never lost to Georgia State.

The Dukes (6-0, 3-0 Sun Belt) host the Panthers (4-1, 1-0) at noon ET on ESPNU with both streaks at stake. JMU is 3-0 at Bridgeforth Stadium and 3-0 on the road, and it survived a 27-24 game at Georgia Southern last weekend. In the series, James Madison is 5-0, most recently a 14-7 win in 2025.

Billy Napier, in his first season at JMU, has a balanced offense. Camden Coleman, the listed starter, has thrown for 1,150 yards with 11 touchdowns and one interception. JC Evans, who started the opener, returned briefly last week, but nothing newer points to a change. George Pettaway leads the ground game with 648 yards and six touchdowns, and Corey Scott has four touchdown catches.

Georgia State has had two weeks to prepare since a 42-10 win over Old Dominion on Oct. 3. Quarterback Cameran Brown has 1,157 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and four interceptions, and Rodshaun Dorsey has turned 18 catches into six touchdowns. Lanear McCrary Jr. leads the rushers with 361 yards. On defense, Xavier Esqillion has seven sacks, which could test JMU's protection. The Panthers' only loss came 44-30 at UCF.

ESPN's Football Power Index sees two similar offenses: Georgia State ranks 41st in efficiency and JMU 38th. The defenses are a step behind, with JMU 73rd and Georgia State 87th, so both teams should be able to move the ball.

These programs are young by college football standards. Georgia State played its first season in 2010 under Bill Curry. James Madison's history goes back to 1972, and its list of coaches includes Mickey Matthews and Curt Cignetti. The Dukes won the Sun Belt title in 2025.

The forecast calls for gusts near 23 mph and a chance of rain, which could tilt things toward JMU's running game.

Both teams have a lot at stake. JMU visits Appalachian State on Oct. 22. Georgia State goes to Arkansas State next week.

Our score assumes Coleman starts, since he is the listed starter and nothing newer says otherwise. With Coleman, we see James Madison 35, Georgia State 25. If Evans were to start, it would look more like James Madison 33, Georgia State 26.

Our call: James Madison 35, Georgia State 25.

fanatic_story.headline: Two Big Ten Teams Searching in the Wind
fanatic_story.dek: Rutgers and Maryland are both winless in the league, and gusty weather in College Park adds another twist to a series Rutgers has won two straight
fanatic_story.body:
COLLEGE PARK, Md. — Somebody is getting off the schneid in the Big Ten today.

Rutgers (1-4, 0-2) visits Maryland (2-4, 0-3) at 12:30 p.m. ET on BTN in a matchup of teams still looking for their first league win. The Terrapins have lost four straight, most recently 45-16 at No. 4 Ohio State. Rutgers has lost four of five and had an open week after a 47-15 loss to Indiana on Oct. 4.

The best player on the field may be Rutgers receiver KJ Duff, who has 33 catches for 628 yards and seven touchdowns. Quarterback Dylan Lonergan, who left the Indiana game, is back practicing, and Greg Schiano says he will start. He has thrown seven touchdowns and five interceptions. Antwan Raymond leads the rushers with 469 yards.

Maryland's offense runs on volume. Malik Washington has completed 136 of 223 passes for 1,352 yards, with seven touchdowns and six interceptions, and Chris Durr Jr. has 46 catches. Mike Locksley, in his eighth season, needs a spark, and the matchup might provide one: ESPN's Football Power Index ranks Rutgers' defense 118th in efficiency, and Rutgers is missing several defensive backs. Ty Morris and Rondo Porter are doubtful, and receiver Jourdin Houston is a game-time decision.

Maryland's defense, 45th in ESPN's index, is the best unit on the field, and Derrick LeBlanc leads it with 2.5 sacks.

Weather could scramble everything. ESPN's forecast calls for gusts near 37 mph and a 47 percent chance of rain, which could limit both passing games.

This has become an annual game. The Big Ten made it a protected annual game in 2024, and Maryland leads the series 12-9. Rutgers has won the past two meetings, including 35-20 last season.

Their histories go back a long way. Rutgers played in the first college football game in 1869 and claims that season's national title. Maryland's high point came under Jim Tatum, whose 1953 team won a national championship. Greg Schiano is in his 18th season at Rutgers across two stints.

After this, the schedule doesn't ease up. Rutgers visits No. 25 Northwestern next week, and Maryland hosts Illinois on Oct. 31.

Rutgers' rest and Duff's big plays should keep it close. Maryland's home field and a short-handed Rutgers secondary are the difference.

Our call: Maryland 29, Rutgers 24.

fanatic_story.headline: The Corps Meets the Corps at Kyle Field
fanatic_story.dek: Texas A&M looks to regroup against FCS The Citadel before a trip to Alabama, in a matchup of two schools with deep military traditions
fanatic_story.body:
COLLEGE STATION, Texas — Two schools with proud military traditions meet at Kyle Field, and only one of them seats 102,733.

Texas A&M (3-3, 1-3 SEC) hosts FCS The Citadel (2-4) at 1 p.m. ET on SEC Network+. The Aggies need a lift after a 27-6 loss at No. 13 Missouri last Saturday, their third SEC defeat. Next week they visit No. 6 Alabama.

This is only the second meeting between the programs. Texas A&M won the first one, 35-3, at Kyle Field on Sept. 2, 2006.

Mike Elko, in his third season, has a defense-first team with an offense still finding its rhythm. Quarterback Marcel Reed has completed 104 of 188 passes for 1,097 yards, with six touchdowns and six interceptions. Rueben Owens II leads the rushers with 304 yards, and Isaiah Horton has three touchdown catches.

The Citadel brings a run game that can shorten any afternoon. Gavin Garcia has carried 111 times for 579 yards and six touchdowns, and Zyion Brown leads the defense in both tackles (51) and sacks (four). Quarterback Quentin Hayes has thrown four touchdown passes. The Bulldogs have been in tight games all season, including a triple-overtime win at Charlotte and a double-overtime loss to Charleston Southern, and they fell 34-16 to East Tennessee State last week.

The gap in resources is large. Kyle Field seats 102,733. The Citadel's Johnson Hagood Stadium seats 11,427. But the Bulldogs, coached by Maurice Drayton, have an option-based offense that can keep the ball away from an opponent if it stays on schedule.

Texas A&M's tradition includes national titles claimed for 1919, 1927 and 1939, and Heisman Trophy winners John David Crow (1957) and Johnny Manziel (2012). The Citadel has four Southern Conference titles, the most recent in 2016.

Wind could matter early, with gusts near 27 mph, but the forecast is otherwise clear at 63 degrees. Neither team listed injuries of note.

For the Aggies, the goal is simple: clean execution, a healthy roster and some confidence before Tuscaloosa. For The Citadel, it's a chance to measure itself against an SEC program.

Our call: Texas A&M 50, The Citadel 6.

fanatic_story.headline: UMass Turns to Its Third Quarterback
fanatic_story.dek: With Pop Watson and Aedan McCarthy both out, Logan Inagawa makes his first FBS start as UMass tries to end a three-game skid against Buffalo
fanatic_story.body:
BUFFALO, N.Y. — UMass will start its third-string quarterback in a MAC game it badly needs.

The Minutemen (4-2, 1-2 MAC) visit Buffalo (3-3, 1-1) at 1 p.m. ET on ESPN+ without starter William "Pop" Watson, who is out with an ankle injury, or backup Aedan McCarthy, also ruled out. That leaves Logan Inagawa, who will make his first FBS start, according to the Greenfield Recorder.

Watson had been efficient, completing 74 of 100 passes for 820 yards with seven touchdowns and two interceptions. Without him, UMass will probably lean on Curtis Kimmons IV, who has four rushing touchdowns, and receiver T.Y. Harding, who has 28 catches. Timmy Hinspeter leads the defense with 51 tackles.

UMass started 4-0 against a soft early schedule before losing 38-14 to Eastern Michigan and 20-19 to Miami (Ohio). Joe Harasymiak is in his second season, and a 4-2 start is real progress.

Buffalo is coming off its best performance of the year, a 23-8 win at Toledo. Pete Lembo's offense is built on running back Messiah Burch, who has 489 yards, and receiver Chance Morrow, who has six touchdown catches. Quarterback Jason Wright has completed 63 of 129 passes for 726 yards.

Neither offense moves the ball easily. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks UMass's offense 115th in efficiency and Buffalo's 124th, while the UMass defense, at 91st, is the best unit on the field. Expect long drives, short fields deciding things and a premium on turnovers.

Buffalo has won the last three meetings, including a 28-21 win on Oct. 18, 2025, and leads the series 10-6.

The forecast is cool and dry: 46 degrees at Broadview Stadium with light wind.

The histories are different. UMass has played football since 1879 and won many Yankee Conference titles. Buffalo's high point remains Turner Gill's 2008 MAC championship, still the program's only league crown.

Our score assumes Inagawa starts because Watson and McCarthy are both ruled out. With Inagawa, we see Buffalo 23, Massachusetts 17. If Watson were able to play, it would tighten to something like Buffalo 22, Massachusetts 19.

Our call: Buffalo 23, Massachusetts 17.

fanatic_story.headline: The Victory Cannon Is Back on the Table
fanatic_story.dek: Western Michigan brings a 2-0 MAC record to Mount Pleasant, where Central Michigan is unbeaten at home and Angel Flores carries the offense
fanatic_story.body:
MOUNT PLEASANT, Mich. — The Victory Cannon sits in Kalamazoo. Central Michigan wants it back.

Western Michigan (4-2, 2-0 MAC) visits Central Michigan (3-3, 1-1) at 1:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+ in the latest chapter of the state's MAC rivalry. Western won last year's game 24-21 and leads the all-time series 54-40-2. In the Victory Cannon trophy era, the Broncos lead 11-7.

The Broncos are rolling. They've won three of their last four, including a 38-7 win over Kent State last week. Quarterback Broc Lowry has completed 95 of 139 passes for 996 yards, with seven touchdowns and only one interception. Jalen Buckley has run for 392 yards and five scores. Dillon Moore leads the defense in tackles (39) and sacks (2.5). Lance Taylor, in his fourth season, has built a steady team.

Central Michigan's offense has one engine: quarterback Angel Flores. He leads the team in rushing with 501 yards and four touchdowns, and he has thrown for 313 yards. Langston Lewis is the top receiver. Matt Drinkall, in his second season, has the Chippewas 3-0 at Kelly/Shorts Stadium, though they lost 31-14 at Ohio last week.

ESPN's Football Power Index ranks Central's offense 131st in efficiency, against a Western defense ranked 80th. Western's offense ranks 82nd, against a Central defense ranked 99th. Western is the more complete team, but rivalry games don't always follow the numbers. Central's defense will need Jaxon Cherry, who has three sacks, and Mayson Hitchens, who leads the team with 41 tackles, to have big afternoons. Western needs Lowry to keep protecting the football the way he has all season.

Western Michigan claims MAC titles in 1966, 1988, 2016 and 2025. Al Molde and P.J. Fleck are among its best-known coaches. Central Michigan has won seven MAC titles, plus a 1974 Division II national championship.

The forecast is dry and 52 degrees, with gusts near 16 mph. Western's Micah Davis is a game-time decision. Neither team has a key starter ruled out.

The winner gets the cannon and a big step in the MAC race. Western visits Toledo next week, and Central hosts Miami (Ohio).

Western's steadier passing and a defense built to contain Flores are the difference, though the home crowd should keep it close.

Our call: Western Michigan 25, Central Michigan 16.

fanatic_story.dek: Georgia has won nine straight in the Deep South's Oldest Rivalry, and Alex Golesh's rested Auburn team arrives in Athens trying to change that
fanatic_story.body:
ATHENS, Ga. — Georgia just won at Alabama. Now comes the oldest rivalry in the Deep South.

No. 1 Georgia (6-0, 4-0 SEC) hosts Auburn (3-2, 1-2) at 3:30 p.m. ET on ESPN in the 131st meeting of a series that began on Feb. 20, 1892, when Auburn won 10-0. Georgia leads 66-56-8 and has won nine straight, including 20-10 last season.

Kirby Smart, in his 11th season, has the nation's top offense by ESPN's efficiency measure. Quarterback Gunner Stockton has completed 95 of 124 passes, more than 76 percent, for 1,298 yards, with 14 touchdowns and two interceptions. Georgia beat Alabama 20-17 in Tuscaloosa last week. The defense, led by Raylen Wilson, ranks 12th.

The Bulldogs are banged up, though. KJ Bolden is out, along with several receivers on the reserve list.

Auburn comes in rested after an open week. Alex Golesh, in his first season, has a quarterback who can hurt defenses two ways: Byrum Brown has thrown for 1,055 yards and run for 344 more, with four rushing touchdowns. He has also thrown seven interceptions, and that's a dangerous number against a defense this good. Keshaun Singleton leads the receivers with 29 catches. Auburn's defense, 23rd in ESPN's efficiency index, will be without sack leader Xavier Atkins. Elijah Melendez, who has 43 tackles, has to be everywhere. For the Tigers to pull off an upset, they likely need to win the turnover battle and keep Stockton off the field with long drives.

Jamal Roberts gives Eliah Drinkwitz's offense balance with 828 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, and Cayden Lee has 616 receiving yards.

Ole Miss counters with offense. Trinidad Chambliss has completed 122 of 174 passes for 1,435 yards and 11 touchdowns, though he has thrown four interceptions. Deuce Alexander has 503 receiving yards, and Kewan Lacy has five rushing touchdowns. ESPN ranks the Rebels' offense 14th in efficiency. Our call: Ole Miss 31, Missouri 26.
