KNOXVILLE, Tenn. — For once, the Third Saturday in October falls on the third Saturday in October.

No. 6 Alabama (5-1, 3-1 SEC) visits No. 14 Tennessee (5-1, 2-1) at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC in the 109th meeting of a rivalry that began in 1901 with a 6-6 tie. Alabama leads the series 60-40-8 and won last year's game 37-20.

Both teams have one loss, and both came by three points. Alabama fell 20-17 to No. 1 Georgia last week. Tennessee lost 20-17 to Texas on Sept. 26.

The biggest news is Tennessee's quarterback. George MacIntyre has been named the starter over Faizon Brandon, who is off the injury report. It will be MacIntyre's second career start, and it comes against a defense ESPN's Football Power Index ranks fifth in efficiency. Brandon has thrown for 697 yards and seven touchdowns this season.

Tennessee's offense will lean on DeSean Bishop, who has 678 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, and Mike Matthews, who has 396 receiving yards. Josh Heupel, in his sixth season, has a defense ranked eighth under Jim Knowles, and Xavier Gilliam has five sacks.

Alabama's offense ranks third in ESPN's index. Keelon Russell has completed 110 of 162 passes for 1,599 yards, with 12 touchdowns and two interceptions. But the Tide are without leading receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams, along with Racin Delgatty and Terrance Green. Trae'shawn Brown has five rushing touchdowns, and Luke Metz leads the defense with 43 tackles. Kalen DeBoer is in his third season, and his team has scored at least 45 points in four of its last five games. The question is whether that pace holds up in Knoxville without its top receiver.

Neyland Stadium seats 101,915 and will be full. The weather should be dry and 57 degrees, with gusts near 18 mph.

Both programs have championship pedigrees. Alabama claims 18 national titles, with Bear Bryant and Nick Saban building most of them. Tennessee's most recent title came in 1998 under Phillip Fulmer.

Alabama hosts Texas A&M next week, and Tennessee visits South Carolina.

Our score assumes MacIntyre starts because he was named the starter. With MacIntyre, we see Alabama 28, Tennessee 20. If Brandon were to start instead, we'd expect something closer: Alabama 27, Tennessee 22.

Our call: Alabama 28, Tennessee 20.

Arizona State, the 2024 Big 12 champion, has had an up-and-down season. The Sun Devils lost 48-20 at Texas A&M and 55-19 to Baylor. Quarterback Cutter Boley has 1,229 yards, 12 touchdowns and three interceptions, and Reed Harris is his top target with 590 yards and seven touchdowns. Owen Long leads the defense with 48 tackles. fanatic_story.headline: Northern Illinois Seeks a First Win at Altitude
fanatic_story.dek: The 0-5 Huskies, under interim coach Rob Harley, visit a Wyoming team coming off an overtime win, in only the third meeting between the schools
fanatic_story.body:
LARAMIE, Wyo. — Northern Illinois is still waiting on its first win. Laramie, at more than 7,000 feet, isn't an easy place to find one.

The Huskies (0-5, 0-1 Mountain West) visit Wyoming (3-3, 2-1) at 3:30 p.m. ET on The CW. Northern Illinois is in its first season under interim coach Rob Harley and has scored more than 17 points only once. Wyoming won 16-13 in overtime at San José State last week.

This is only the third meeting between the programs. Wyoming won both of the first two: 40-34 in triple overtime in Laramie in 2016, and 50-43 in DeKalb in 2021.

Neither offense has found much. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks Northern Illinois 126th in offensive efficiency and Wyoming 133rd. The defenses aren't much better, at 108th for the Huskies and 117th for the Cowboys.

Northern Illinois quarterback Taron Dickens has completed 97 of 140 passes, almost 70 percent, for 977 yards, with three touchdowns and three interceptions. DeAree Rogers has 38 catches, and Telly Johnson Jr. has three rushing touchdowns. Kyon Conyers leads the defense with 36 tackles. The Huskies lost 28-24 to FCS Illinois State and 28-7 to Air Force last week.

Wyoming's Tyler Hughes has thrown for 822 yards but with three touchdowns and seven interceptions. Samuel Harris leads the rushers with 324 yards. Jones Thomas has 42 tackles, and Esaia Bogar has 3.5 sacks. Jay Sawvel, in his third season, has the Cowboys 2-0 at War Memorial Stadium.

Wyoming has a defense-first identity, and its 14 conference titles include seven from the Skyline Conference. Northern Illinois has won the MAC six times, most recently in 2021, with Jerry Kill and Dave Doeren among its program-builders.

The weather should be dry and 66 degrees, with gusts near 21 mph. Neither team listed injuries of note, so turnovers and field position probably decide it. Hughes's seven interceptions are the number Northern Illinois's defense will target, and Dickens's accuracy is the Huskies' best path to sustained drives.

Wyoming hosts Air Force next week. Northern Illinois hosts Hawai'i.

Home field, altitude and a better defense give Wyoming the edge, but Northern Illinois's defense should keep it close.

Our call: Wyoming 24, Northern Illinois 18.

UNLV (4-2, 2-0 Mountain West) visits Air Force (4-1, 2-1) at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS Sports Network. Air Force lost quarterback Liam Szarka for the season on Oct. 3. Sophomore Evan Medders made his first start last week in a 28-7 win at Northern Illinois. Szarka had been the Falcons' leading rusher, with 391 yards and seven touchdowns.

UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold is questionable with an undisclosed issue, and nothing has downgraded him. He has completed 87 of 149 passes for 1,140 yards, with eight touchdowns and one interception. If he can't go, Alex Orji, who made three starts at Michigan in 2024, would take over.

UNLV's defense is the best unit in the game. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks it 34th in efficiency, and it just held North Dakota State to seven points in a 13-7 win. Jake Pope has 48 tackles, and Tre Fulton has 3.5 sacks. Jai'Den Thomas leads the offense with 495 rushing yards. Dan Mullen, in his second season, has the Rebels unbeaten in league play.

Air Force's triple option, run by coordinator Mike Thiessen, depends on the quarterback reading defenders to decide who carries the ball. The Falcons rank 65th in offensive efficiency. Blake Fletcher leads the defense with 54 tackles. Troy Calhoun, in his 20th season, has the Falcons 4-1, including wins over Navy (14-9) and Nevada (36-33 in double overtime).

Our call: UNLV 23, Air Force 22.

Connor Walendzak has seven rushing touchdowns, and Adjatay Dabbs leads the receivers with 402 yards. On defense, Andrew Zock has five sacks, and Armorion Smith has 51 tackles. Amareon Blue leads the rushers with 315 yards, and Benson Prosper has 28 catches. Quincy Byas has four sacks, and Zach Mowchan has 51 tackles. fanatic_story.headline: Miami's Deep Shots Meet a Searching Akron Defense
fanatic_story.dek: The RedHawks have won eight straight against Akron, and David McComb's big-play passing leads the MAC afternoon in Oxford
fanatic_story.body:
OXFORD, Ohio — Miami has owned this series for most of a decade. Akron arrives hoping close losses turn into a breakthrough.

Akron (1-5, 0-2 MAC) visits Miami (3-3, 1-1) at 3:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+. The Zips have lost five straight, though last week's 25-23 loss to Eastern Michigan was their closest. Miami won 20-19 at UMass.

Miami leads the series 24-9-1 and has won eight straight since 2017, most recently 20-7 in Akron on Oct. 11, 2025.

Miami quarterback David McComb has completed 65 of 103 passes for 1,121 yards, more than 17 yards per completion, with seven touchdowns and one interception. Maleek Huggins is his deep threat with 309 receiving yards. Malcolm McCain leads the defense with 48 tackles, and Roosevelt Andrews III has three sacks. Chuck Martin is in his 13th season.

Akron's quarterback picture is unsettled. Cibastian Broughton is day-to-day with a knee injury after missing three straight games, and Brayden Roggow has started each of them. Roggow has thrown for 834 yards with six touchdowns and four interceptions. Jordan Gant leads the rushers with 410 yards, and Donelius Johnson has 57 tackles. Joe Moorhead, in his fifth season, runs the offense himself, and his up-tempo approach could produce extra possessions against a Miami defense that has given up yards. Akron has lost by 24 or more three times this season, but it has also shown it can stay close.

ESPN's Football Power Index ranks Akron's defense 133rd in efficiency, against a Miami offense ranked 71st. Miami's defense ranks 128th, so Akron's offense, at 108th, should have some chances.

Miami is known as the Cradle of Coaches. Sid Gillman, Ara Parseghian, Bo Schembechler and Bill Mallory all coached there, and the RedHawks won the MAC in 2019 and 2023. Akron's lone MAC title came in 2005.

The weather should be dry and 53 degrees with light wind at Yager Stadium.

Both teams play MAC road games next week: Akron at Kent State and Miami at Central Michigan.

Our score assumes Roggow starts, since Broughton has missed three straight games. With Roggow, we see Miami 31, Akron 19. If Broughton returns, it's about the same: Miami 30, Akron 20.

Miami's big-play passing against a struggling defense, plus home field, is the difference.

Our call: Miami (OH) 31, Akron 19.

fanatic_story.headline: Baylor Hayes Returns as Tulsa Visits Rice
fanatic_story.dek: Both teams are winless in the American, and Tulsa gets its starting quarterback back for the 20th meeting of an old Southwest series
fanatic_story.body:
HOUSTON — Someone gets a first conference win tonight.

Tulsa (3-3, 0-2 American) visits Rice (1-5, 0-2) at 4:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Tulsa has lost three straight, including a 45-44 overtime loss to North Texas and a 34-26 loss at Navy. Rice has lost five straight, two of them by seven points or fewer.

Tulsa quarterback Baylor Hayes is back and starting. He missed two games earlier in the season with a knee injury. He has thrown for 832 yards with five touchdowns and one interception. Damari Alston has five rushing touchdowns, and Oran Singleton Jr. leads the receivers with 387 yards. Chris Thompson Jr. has 56 tackles, and Thomas Davis has four sacks. Tre Lamb is in his second season. Hayes's return matters because Tulsa's offense stalled without him, and his ball security fits a game where field position may decide things.

Rice runs through Jacurri Brown, who leads the team in passing and rushing. Brown has run for 514 yards and four touchdowns and thrown for 431. AJ Brown leads the defense with 44 tackles. Scott Abell is in his second season as head coach. Brown has completed only 38 of 77 passes, so Tulsa's plan will be to load up against the run and make him beat it through the air.

ESPN's Football Power Index ranks Tulsa's defense 68th in efficiency, against a Rice offense ranked 119th. Tulsa's offense ranks 78th, against a Rice defense ranked 98th.

The series is close. Tulsa leads 10-9-1 in 20 meetings, but Rice has won the past two, including a 42-10 win in Tulsa on Oct. 19, 2023. The teams didn't meet in 2025. The first meeting was a 0-0 tie in 1937.

Rice's history includes seven Southwest Conference titles and a 1954 Cotton Bowl win. Tulsa's history includes John Cooper and Todd Graham, and dozens of Missouri Valley Conference titles.

The forecast calls for 71 degrees and dry weather, with gusts near 22 mph.

Tulsa hosts Army on Oct. 23. Rice visits Florida Atlantic next week.

Tulsa's better offense and defense, plus Hayes's return, give the Golden Hurricane the edge. Rice's home field and Brown's running should keep it close.

Neither offense has many explosive plays, so this should be a modest-scoring game decided by a few possessions.

Our call: Tulsa 26, Rice 20.

fanatic_story.headline: Oregon State's Air Show Meets a First-Time Starter
fanatic_story.dek: Washington State turns to redshirt freshman Owen Eshelman against Braden Atkinson and an Oregon State offense ranked ninth nationally
fanatic_story.body:
CORVALLIS, Ore. — Oregon State scored 66 points last week. Washington State is starting a quarterback who has never started a college game.

Washington State (1-5, 0-2) visits Oregon State (4-2, 2-0) at 6 p.m. ET on USA Network at Reser Stadium. The Cougars have lost four straight, including a 17-16 loss at Utah State last week. Coach Kirby Moore benched Caden Pinnick for redshirt freshman Owen Eshelman, who makes his first career start. It was a coaching choice, not an injury.

Pinnick had completed 110 of 178 passes for 952 yards with three touchdowns and five interceptions. Kirby Vorhees leads the rushers with 251 yards, and Darrius Clemons has 20 catches. Keith Brown has 36 tackles.

Oregon State's offense is one of the best in the country. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks it ninth in efficiency. Braden Atkinson has completed 166 of 235 passes, more than 70 percent, for 2,257 yards, with 21 touchdowns and two interceptions. Jesse Legree has 932 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns. Takari Hickle has 3.5 sacks, and Aiden Sullivan has 42 tackles. JaMarcus Shephard is in his first season as head coach.

Washington State's defense ranks 56th, and its offense ranks 129th against an Oregon State defense ranked 46th. Eshelman will need help from his run game, and Jirah Leaupepetele, who leads the Cougars with 2.5 sacks, will need to pressure Atkinson.

The series is long and lopsided toward the Cougars. Washington State leads 58-49-3 in 110 meetings since 1903. The teams split two games in 2025: Oregon State won 10-7 in Corvallis on Nov. 1, and Washington State won 32-8 in Pullman on Nov. 29.

These are the two programs that stayed together when the old Pac-12 broke apart. Washington State's history includes Mike Price and Mike Leach. Oregon State's Terry Baker won the Heisman Trophy in 1962.

The weather should be calm and 68 degrees, with a small chance of rain.

Washington State hosts No. 23 Boise State next week. Oregon State gets an open week before visiting Fresno State.

Oregon State's offense against a first-time starter gives the Beavers a clear edge on paper.

Our call: Oregon State 35, Washington State 16.

tailgate.line: Measure twice, kick once. People think Oregon State is rebuilding. Braden Atkinson has 21 touchdowns and two interceptions. That's an old-growth offense, rooted deep.

tailgate.speaker: Juniper Ostrowski

tailgate.line: I said 'pine' once, years ago. She still brings it up.

tailgate.speaker: Juniper Ostrowski
tailgate.line: It's on your cassette, Hank.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: *(laughing)* Receipts, please. Washington State leads 58-49-3, and the teams split two games last year.

tailgate.speaker: Hank Palouse
tailgate.line: Thirty-two to eight in Pullman. I have the tape.

tailgate.speaker: Juniper Ostrowski
tailgate.line: And 10-7 in Corvallis. Rooted deep.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: Program pride, one sentence each. Hank?

tailgate.speaker: Hank Palouse
tailgate.line: Mike Price, Mike Leach and a 2025 conference title.

tailgate.speaker: Juniper Ostrowski
tailgate.line: Terry Baker won the Heisman here in 1962, and we never let anybody forget it.

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale
tailgate.line: Juniper, JaMarcus Shephard in year one. Growth rings?

tailgate.speaker: Juniper Ostrowski

tailgate.speaker: Roxy Vale

tailgate.speaker: Hank Palouse

fanatic_story.headline: Two SEC Teams Looking for a First League Win
fanatic_story.dek: Arkansas and Vanderbilt are both 0-3 in conference play, and a Saturday night in Nashville offers one of them a way out
fanatic_story.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. — One of these teams will leave with its first SEC win.

Arkansas (2-4, 0-3 SEC) visits Vanderbilt (3-3, 0-3) at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN2 at FirstBank Stadium. Both teams have had a punishing league schedule. Arkansas lost to Georgia, Texas A&M and, last week, 24-17 to No. 14 Tennessee. Vanderbilt lost at Auburn and Georgia before a 52-17 home loss to No. 9 Ole Miss.

Arkansas, in Ryan Silverfield's first season, runs through quarterback KJ Jackson and receiver Chris Marshall. Jackson has completed 110 of 184 passes for 1,193 yards, with seven touchdowns and four interceptions. Marshall has 42 catches for 605 yards. The run game has been thin, with Sutton Smith leading the team at 166 yards. Ben Bogle has 44 tackles, and Quincy Rhodes Jr. has three sacks.

Vanderbilt quarterback Jared Curtis has thrown for 968 yards with five touchdowns and five interceptions. Junior Sherrill is his top target with 529 yards, and Sedrick Alexander has four rushing touchdowns. CJ Heard has 42 tackles, and Nick Rinaldi has 3.5 sacks. Clark Lea's team is 3-1 at home, with wins over Delaware and NC State. Brian Allen Jr. is probable. For Vanderbilt, the key is cutting down Curtis's interceptions; for Arkansas, it's finding enough of a run game to keep Jackson out of obvious passing downs. Whichever quarterback protects the ball better probably wins.

ESPN's Football Power Index sees two nearly identical teams: Arkansas ranks 61st overall and Vanderbilt 62nd. Arkansas's defense, 64th in efficiency, is a bit better than Vanderbilt's, which ranks 76th. Vanderbilt's offense ranks 88th and Arkansas's 92nd.

These teams don't meet often. Vanderbilt won their 2018 meeting, 45-31.

Arkansas's history includes Frank Broyles's 1964 national championship and Lou Holtz's run from 1977 to 1983. Vanderbilt's best modern stretches came under Bobby Johnson and James Franklin. Several Vanderbilt reserves are out, including backup quarterback Blaze Berlowitz.

The weather should be clear and 58 degrees, with gusts near 18 mph.

The schedule stays tough. Vanderbilt visits No. 15 Kentucky next week. Arkansas gets an open week before hosting No. 13 Missouri.

In a game this even, Vanderbilt's home field gives it the edge.

Our call: Vanderbilt 27, Arkansas 23.

TCU is without linebacker Michael Short, cornerback Devondre McGee and two offensive linemen, and kicker Kyle Lemmermann is questionable. Tight end Kari Ashley, with 374 yards and four touchdowns, is probable for the Frogs. Mild weather makes this a test of defense.

fanatic_story.headline: The Bluebonnet Battle Returns to Waco
fanatic_story.dek: Baylor is unbeaten in the Big 12 and rested, while TCU's top-25 defense tries to keep a 2-3 season from slipping away
fanatic_story.body:
WACO, Texas — Baylor is 2-0 in the Big 12. TCU is 0-2. And the Bluebonnet Battle rarely cares about records.

TCU (2-3, 0-2) visits Baylor (4-1, 2-0) at 7 p.m. ET on FS1 at McLane Stadium in the 122nd meeting of a series that dates to 1899. Both teams are coming off open weeks. TCU won last year's game 42-36.

Baylor's last game was its best, a 55-19 win at Arizona State on Oct. 4. Quarterback DJ Lagway has thrown for 860 yards with eight touchdowns and two interceptions, and Gavin Freeman leads the receivers with 42 catches. Dawson Pendergrass leads the rushers with 316 yards. Travion Barnes has 33 tackles, and Daniel Cobbs has three sacks. Dave Aranda, in his seventh season, has the Bears 3-0 at home.

TCU's defense is the best unit on the field. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks it 22nd in efficiency, and the Frogs have allowed 17 or fewer points in all three losses. The problem is offense. TCU has scored 15, 13 and 10 points in those defeats. Quarterback Jaden Craig has completed 108 of 157 passes for 1,400 yards, with eight touchdowns and four interceptions. Ed Small has 403 receiving yards, and Jeremy Payne has 432 rushing yards. TCU is missing several players, and kicker Kyle Lemmermann is a game-time decision.

Baylor's defense ranks 31st, so points may be hard to find for both teams. TCU's best hope is a short field: turnovers, special teams and long, clock-eating drives with Payne. Baylor, meanwhile, will want Lagway to keep taking care of the ball, as he has all season. Baylor's offense ranks 56th, and TCU's ranks 94th.

The tradition runs deep. TCU claims national titles in 1935 and 1938, and Davey O'Brien won the Heisman Trophy in 1938. Baylor's program was built by Grant Teaff, and Robert Griffin III won the Heisman in 2011. Baylor won Big 12 titles in 2013, 2014 and 2021.

The forecast calls for clear skies and 66 degrees with light wind.

TCU hosts West Virginia next week. Baylor visits Kansas.

Baylor's home field and healthier roster give it the edge, while TCU's defense should keep the score down.

Our call: Baylor 27, TCU 20.

Ashton Daniels is available, and Ousmane Kromah has 565 rushing yards.

Florida State's biggest problem is linebacker. Blake Nichelson, Izayia Williams, Daylen Green and Noah LaVallee are all out, along with three defensive backs. Miami is missing receiver Joshua Moore, running back CharMar Brown and two defensive backs. FSU lost 44-20 at Louisville last week. Warm weather should allow plenty of offense.

fanatic_story.headline: Unbeaten Miami Hosts Florida State on a Wet Night
fanatic_story.dek: No. 3 Miami and nearly perfect Darian Mensah face a Florida State defense missing several key players, with rain in the forecast at Hard Rock Stadium
fanatic_story.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. — Miami has been almost flawless. Florida State would love to be the team that changes that.

Florida State (3-3, 1-2 ACC) visits No. 3 Miami (5-0, 3-0) at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN and Disney+ in the 71st meeting of one of college football's fiercest rivalries. Miami leads the series 37-33 and has won the last two, including 28-22 last season.

Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has completed 112 of 133 passes, about 84 percent, for 1,438 yards with 15 touchdowns and no interceptions. Malachi Toney has 39 catches for 604 yards and six touchdowns. Mark Fletcher Jr. has five rushing touchdowns, and Marquise Lightfoot has five sacks. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks Miami's offense second in efficiency and its defense 10th. Mario Cristobal, in his fifth season, has the Hurricanes rested after a 41-13 win at Clemson on Oct. 3.

Florida State has been inconsistent. The Seminoles beat Virginia 38-7, then lost 44-20 at Louisville on Oct. 9. Quarterback Michael Van Buren Jr. has completed 93 of 152 passes for 1,073 yards with five touchdowns and no interceptions. Bryson Rodgers leads the receivers with 27 catches. Ayden Jackson has 37 tackles, and Michael Williams II has 2.5 sacks.

Kent State has struggled to score. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks the Golden Flashes' offense 132nd in efficiency. Quarterback Dru DeShields has thrown for 980 yards with four touchdowns and six interceptions. Wayne Harris has 368 receiving yards, and Mason King leads the rushers with 202 yards. Rocco Nicholl has three sacks, and Joel Cordoba has 30 tackles. Mark Carney is in his second season, his first after being promoted from interim coach.

USF's offense ranks 73rd in ESPN's index, against a Kent defense ranked 102nd. The Bulls' defense ranks 93rd.

The histories are short and long. South Florida played its first season in 1997 under Jim Leavitt. Kent State has played since 1920, and its lone MAC title came in 1972 under Don James.

The weather should be warm and mostly dry, 70 degrees with gusts near 24 mph. Neither team listed injuries of note.

Kent State hosts Akron next week. South Florida gets an open week before hosting UAB on Oct. 31.

USF's run game should control the clock, and Kent's offensive struggles make it hard for the Flashes to keep pace. Van Buren's ball security is a big part of the plan: he hasn't thrown an interception all season, and a homecoming crowd should give the Bulls another lift.

Our call: South Florida 32, Kent State 10.

fanatic_story.dek: No. 15 Kentucky has won two straight in overtime, and now Will Stein's Wildcats face Oklahoma's fourth-ranked defense in Norman
fanatic_story.body:
NORMAN, Okla. — Kentucky has lived on the edge for two weeks. Oklahoma's defense doesn't usually leave much room for that.

No. 15 Kentucky (5-1, 3-1 SEC) visits Oklahoma (3-2, 1-1) at 7:30 p.m. ET on SEC Network. The Wildcats beat South Carolina and LSU by identical 35-34 overtime scores. Oklahoma is coming off a 27-24 win over No. 7 Texas in Dallas.

Kentucky, in Will Stein's first season, has one of the SEC's most efficient quarterbacks. Kenny Minchey has completed 120 of 178 passes for 1,394 yards, with 11 touchdowns and one interception. CJ Baxter has eight rushing touchdowns but is a game-time decision. Kenny Darby leads the receivers with 401 yards. Grant Godfrey has 52 tackles. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks Kentucky's offense 21st in efficiency.

That offense meets Oklahoma's defense, which ESPN ranks fourth. Owen Heinecke leads the Sooners with 36 tackles. Brent Venables, in his fifth season, has a team that has allowed six points to New Mexico and 10 to Michigan.

The Sooners' offense has been less reliable, ranked 85th in efficiency. John Mateer has thrown for 1,038 yards with eight touchdowns and four interceptions, and Isaiah Sategna III leads the receivers with 331 yards. Oklahoma is also short-handed: Eli Bowen and Parker Livingstone are out, and several players up front, including Eddy Pierre-Louis, are doubtful.

Kentucky's defense, ranked 27th, should give Mateer trouble too.

These programs have met only three times. Kentucky won the first, 13-7, in the 1951 Sugar Bowl. Oklahoma won 29-7 in Norman in 1980 and 29-8 in Lexington in 1982.

That Sugar Bowl is part of why Kentucky claims a 1950 national title, a season Oklahoma also claims. The Sooners' list of titles is long: seven, under coaches including Bud Wilkinson, Barry Switzer and Bob Stoops. Oklahoma has seven Heisman winners, from Billy Vessels in 1952 to Kyler Murray in 2018.

The weather should be calm and 58 degrees.

Kentucky hosts Vanderbilt next week. Oklahoma visits No. 16 Mississippi State.

Oklahoma's defense and home field should be the difference, though the Sooners' issues up front give Kentucky a real chance to keep it close.

Our call: Oklahoma 24, Kentucky 18.

fanatic_story.headline: Elon Goes West for the First Time
fanatic_story.dek: FCS Elon makes its first trip to the West Coast to face a Stanford team trying to bounce back from three lopsided losses
fanatic_story.body:
STANFORD, Calif. — Elon has never played a football game on the West Coast. Tonight it plays one at Stanford Stadium.

FCS Elon (4-3) visits Stanford (2-4) at 7:30 p.m. ET on ACC Network Extra in the first meeting between the schools. It's a chance for Stanford to regroup after losses of 35-7 at Duke, 57-3 at Wake Forest and 58-7 at No. 2 Notre Dame.

Stanford, in Tavita Pritchard's first season, has had trouble finding consistency. Quarterback Davis Warren has completed 114 of 195 passes for 1,351 yards, with six touchdowns and two interceptions. Caden High has three touchdown catches, and Micah Ford has four rushing touchdowns. Matt Rose leads the defense with 38 tackles. The Cardinal's only league win came 34-27 over Georgia Tech.

Elon's offense runs through running back Kamerin McDowell-Moore, who has 137 carries for 916 yards and six touchdowns. The passing game has struggled. Elijah Guttman has completed 36 of 85 passes with two touchdowns and five interceptions. Brady Stober, the opening-day starter, returned last week against Wofford after an injury in the Davidson game, but Elon has used three quarterbacks this season and has not announced a starter. Brodie Carroll leads the defense with 68 tackles. Tony Trisciani is in his eighth season.

The Phoenix were shut out 16-0 by Wofford last week, and they lost 30-23 at New Hampshire before that.

The histories are very different. Stanford claims national titles in 1926 and 1940, Jim Plunkett won the Heisman Trophy in 1970, and Bill Walsh, Jim Harbaugh and David Shaw all coached on the Farm. Elon has won 18 conference titles, many of them in its small-college days.

The weather could be a factor. The forecast calls for 90 degrees, which could wear down a visiting team late.

Stanford gets an open week before hosting NC State on Oct. 23.

Stanford's size and depth advantage over an FCS opponent, plus home field, should be the difference. McDowell-Moore can create a few big plays, but Elon's passing struggles make it hard to keep pace. The real test for Stanford is whether its offense can finally turn a good week of practice into a complete game.

Our call: Stanford 43, Elon 13.

fanatic_story.headline: UCLA Loses Its Quarterback, Gains a Test
fanatic_story.dek: No. 12 UCLA, unbeaten but without Nico Iamaleava, hosts a rested Wisconsin team in the programs' first meeting since the 2000 Sun Bowl
fanatic_story.body:
PASADENA, Calif. — UCLA won at Oregon last week and lost its quarterback in the process. Now Wisconsin comes to the Rose Bowl.

Wisconsin (4-1, 2-0 Big Ten) visits No. 12 UCLA (5-0, 3-0) at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC. The Bruins beat Oregon 17-15, but Nico Iamaleava suffered a season-ending knee injury late in the first half. Ty Dieffenbach takes over.

UCLA, in Bob Chesney's first season, still has its best weapon: running back Wayne Knight, who has 548 yards and 10 touchdowns. Semaj Morgan leads the receivers with 19 catches, and Jalen Woods has 41 tackles. Rodrick Pleasant and Jordan Davis are doubtful. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks UCLA's defense 14th in efficiency.

Wisconsin is rested after an open week following a 31-3 win over Michigan State. Quarterback Colton Joseph has thrown for 1,132 yards with 10 touchdowns and five interceptions, and he leads the team with 262 rushing yards and three scores. Tyrell Henry leads the receivers with 339 yards. Cooper Catalano has 45 tackles. Wisconsin's defense ranks 20th. Luke Fickell has the Badgers unbeaten in league play.

Both defenses are strong and both offenses are average, so expect a low-scoring game. Wisconsin's offense ranks 57th and UCLA's 32nd. The swing factor is Dieffenbach. If UCLA can lean on Knight and keep its new quarterback in comfortable situations, the Bruins can play the field-position game they won at Oregon. Wisconsin's defense, with Sebastian Cheeks leading the pass rush, will try to make him throw on obvious passing downs.

This is the first meeting between the programs since Dec. 29, 2000, when Wisconsin won 21-20 in the Sun Bowl. UCLA leads the series 7-4, but Wisconsin has won the past three, including a 38-31 Rose Bowl win on Jan. 1, 1999.

UCLA's history includes Red Sanders's 1954 national championship and Gary Beban's 1967 Heisman. Wisconsin's includes Barry Alvarez's run from 1990 to 2005, and Heisman winners Alan Ameche and Ron Dayne.

It will be warm in Pasadena, 89 degrees at kickoff time.

Wisconsin hosts No. 19 USC next week. UCLA hosts Michigan State.

UCLA's home field and Knight's running give the Bruins a tiny edge, even with a new quarterback. Wisconsin's rest and defense make it almost a toss-up.

Our call: UCLA 20, Wisconsin 19.

fanatic_story.headline: Navy's Option Meets UTSA's Accuracy for the First Time
fanatic_story.dek: Unbeaten in league play, UTSA hosts Navy in the programs' first meeting, with Jackson Gutierrez now running the Midshipmen's offense
fanatic_story.body:
SAN ANTONIO — Navy and UTSA have never met. The Midshipmen bring a style the Roadrunners rarely see.

Navy (2-3, 1-2 American) visits UTSA (5-1, 2-0) at 8 p.m. ET on ESPNU at the Alamodome. It's the first meeting between the programs, according to UTSA.

Navy's offense, run by coordinator Drew Cronic, is built on misdirection and the run. Jackson Gutierrez, who took over at quarterback, leads the team with 505 rushing yards and seven touchdowns and has thrown four touchdown passes on 47 attempts. Truman Brasfield has two touchdown catches on three receptions. MarcAnthony Parker has four sacks, and Coleman Cauley has 41 tackles. Brian Newberry is in his fourth season as head coach. Navy beat Tulsa 34-26 last week after losing three straight, all by eight points or fewer.

UTSA, under Jeff Traylor, has won four straight. Quarterback Owen McCown has completed 125 of 182 passes, nearly 69 percent, for 1,219 yards with seven touchdowns and two interceptions. Will Henderson III has 484 rushing yards, and Brandon Tucker leads the defense with 46 tackles. The Roadrunners' only loss came 30-6 at Texas. They've won close games against Rice (16-14) and South Florida (31-24).

ESPN's Football Power Index ranks UTSA's offense 72nd in efficiency, against a Navy defense ranked 114th. Navy's offense ranks 91st, against a UTSA defense ranked 66th. The option's real value is time of possession: every long Navy drive is one fewer chance for McCown. UTSA, which plays an up-tempo style, will want to score early and force Navy to throw with a quarterback who has attempted only 47 passes. For Navy, the plan is the usual one: stay ahead of the chains, avoid turnovers and turn the game into a short, physical night. If Navy can keep the score close into the fourth quarter, its misdirection gets more dangerous as a tired defense starts guessing.

Navy's tradition includes Heisman Trophy winners Joe Bellino (1960) and Roger Staubach (1963), and a claimed 1926 national title. UTSA, which played its first season in 2011, won Conference USA titles in 2021 and 2022.

The game is indoors, so weather won't be a factor.

Navy hosts North Texas next week. UTSA visits Tulane.

UTSA's efficient passing against a struggling Navy defense, plus home field, gives the Roadrunners the edge. Navy's option can shorten the game and keep it close.

Our call: UTSA 32, Navy 24.

fanatic_story.headline: The I-20 Rivalry Returns After a Quarter-Century
fanatic_story.dek: Louisiana Tech and ULM meet for the first time since 2000, with the Bulldogs riding two narrow wins and the Warhawks seeking their first
fanatic_story.body:
MONROE, La. — Louisiana Tech and ULM sit about 35 miles apart on Interstate 20. They haven't played football since 2000.

Louisiana Tech (3-2, 1-0) visits UL Monroe (0-5, 0-1) at 8 p.m. ET on ESPN+ at Malone Stadium. The Bulldogs have won two straight close games: 31-29 over Army and 32-31 over Louisiana. ULM is rested after an open week following a 52-35 loss at South Alabama.

The series is old but dormant. The schools have met 43 times, and Louisiana Tech leads 30-13. Tech won the last six meetings, the most recent a 42-19 win on Nov. 11, 2000.

Louisiana Tech quarterback Blake Baker has been efficient, completing 53 of 78 passes for 679 yards with seven touchdowns and one interception. Jalen Mickens has 30 catches for 434 yards, and Alonzo Jackson Jr. has five sacks. Sam Fongang leads the defense with 36 tackles. Sonny Cumbie is in his fifth season.

ULM quarterback Aidan Armenta has thrown for 855 yards with six touchdowns and one interception. Marcellus Jackson leads the receivers with 26 catches, and Noah Flemmings has 43 tackles. Bryant Vincent is in his third season, and ULM is still looking for its first win of 2026. ULM lost 38-35 to Southeastern Louisiana and 26-20 at UAB, but its other three losses came by 17 points or more.

The matchup numbers lean heavily toward Tech. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks ULM's defense 137th in efficiency, the lowest-rated defense in its numbers, against a Tech offense ranked 59th. Tech's defense ranks 62nd, against a ULM offense ranked 113th. ULM's best hope is Armenta's ball security: he has one interception, and a mistake-free night could keep the Warhawks in it. Tech, which has won two straight one-score games, will want a cleaner, earlier lead this time.

Louisiana Tech's history includes Joe Aillet, who coached the Bulldogs for 27 seasons, and WAC titles in 2001 and 2011. ULM won the Sun Belt in 2005.

The weather should be clear and 64 degrees with light wind.

Louisiana Tech hosts Old Dominion next week. ULM visits Troy.

Baker's efficient passing against the lowest-rated defense in ESPN's numbers should be the difference. ULM's rest helps a little.

Our call: Louisiana Tech 38, UL Monroe 21.

San José State (3-3, 1-1 Mountain West) visits UTEP (1-5, 0-2) at 9 p.m. ET on MW+. Spartans quarterback Luke Weaver is questionable after getting hurt against Wyoming, with no game-day downgrade. UTEP's EJ Colson Jr. is questionable with a concussion.

Carson Clark has 37 catches for 405 yards and four touchdowns, and Jabari Bates leads the rushers with 556 yards. Dylan Lee has 53 tackles. Ken Niumatalolo is in his third season. The Spartans lost 16-13 in overtime to Wyoming last week.

UTEP has lost five straight since an opening win over Texas Southern, including 61-7 at New Mexico and 30-13 to Nevada. Colson has thrown for 541 yards with seven touchdowns and three interceptions. Raymond Moore III averages more than seven yards per carry, and Carver Cheeks has three touchdown catches. Isaiah Bogerty leads the defense with 39 tackles. 

Neither offense has been explosive. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks San José State's offense 128th in efficiency and UTEP's 135th. San José State's defense, ranked 75th, is the best unit in the game. Expect both teams to lean on their running backs, especially if either quarterback is limited.

These programs haven't met since Oct. 30, 2004, when UTEP won 38-20 at San José State.

San José State's history includes a 2020 Mountain West title. UTEP, in its first Mountain West season, plays in the Sun Bowl, where Mike Price coached the Miners for nine seasons.

The weather should be clear and 61 degrees.

San José State visits Nevada next week. UTEP gets an open week before visiting North Dakota State.

Our score assumes both quarterbacks play, since both are questionable with no downgrade. With both, we see San José State 25, UTEP 17. If Weaver sits, it would be closer: San José State 23, UTEP 18. If Colson sits, the model sees San José State 26, UTEP 15.

San José State's defense is the difference against a UTEP offense that has struggled.

Our call: San José State 25, UTEP 17.

fanatic_story.dek: The unbeaten-in-league Bobcats make the long trip west for the programs' first meeting, at Sacramento State's homecoming
fanatic_story.body:
SACRAMENTO, Calif. — Ohio is 2-0 in the MAC and has its quarterback back. Sacramento State is looking for a homecoming spark.

Ohio (4-2, 2-0 MAC) visits Sacramento State (1-5, 0-3) at 10 p.m. ET on ESPN+ at Hornet Stadium. It's the first meeting between the programs, and homecoming for the Hornets.

Ohio quarterback Nick Poulos returned on Oct. 10 after missing three games with a concussion, and the Bobcats beat Central Michigan 31-14. Matt Vezza, who started in his absence, has completed 40 of 58 passes for 439 yards. Riley Neer has five touchdown catches, and Victor Rosa has four rushing touchdowns. Ike Ackerman has 4.5 sacks, and Michael Molnar leads the defense with 49 tackles. John Hauser is in his first full season as head coach. Ohio has won three straight, including a 13-10 grinder at Kent State.

Sacramento State has lost four straight since a 52-0 win over Mississippi Valley State. Jackson Sharman has thrown for 1,001 yards with six touchdowns and five interceptions, and Matt Coleman has 454 receiving yards. Boogsie Silvera leads the defense with 42 tackles. Alonzo Carter is in his first season.

The numbers lean hard toward Ohio. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks Sacramento State's offense 138th in efficiency, the lowest in its numbers, against an Ohio defense ranked 111th. Ohio's offense ranks 90th, against a Hornets defense ranked 136th.

Ohio's history includes Frank Solich, who built the Bobcats into a consistent MAC contender, and the 2024 MAC title. Sacramento State won Big Sky titles in 2019, 2021 and 2022.

The game kicks off at 7 p.m. local time, and it should be warm, 79 degrees with almost no wind. The travel and time change are the Hornets' biggest edge.

Ohio hosts Eastern Michigan next week. Sacramento State visits Ball State.

Ohio's balance and the return of its quarterback should control the game. The Bobcats have allowed 14 or fewer points in three of their last four games, and Sacramento State has scored 10 or fewer in four straight. For the Hornets, a homecoming crowd and a fast start are the best recipe.

Our call: Ohio 31, Sacramento State 14.

fanatic_story.headline: Utah Brings Its Perfect Start to Boulder
fanatic_story.dek: No. 11 Utah, unbeaten in Morgan Scalley's first full season, visits a rested Colorado team a year after a 53-7 rout in the Rumble in the Rockies
fanatic_story.body:
BOULDER, Colo. — Colorado has had two weeks to think about last October. Utah is still unbeaten.

No. 11 Utah (5-0, 2-0 Big 12) visits Colorado (2-3, 0-2) at 10:15 p.m. ET on ESPN in the 73rd Rumble in the Rockies. The series began in 1903 with a 22-0 Colorado win. Last season, Utah won 53-7, its most lopsided win in the series.

Utah, in Morgan Scalley's first full season, has the nation's seventh-ranked offense by ESPN's Football Power Index. Devon Dampier has completed 94 of 131 passes for 1,134 yards, with 12 touchdowns and two interceptions. Wayshawn Parker averages more than seven yards per carry and has seven rushing touchdowns, and Braden Pegan has four touchdown catches. Utah's defense ranks 26th, and Trey Reynolds leads it with 32 tackles. The Utes beat Kansas 41-24 last week.

Colorado has lost three straight after a 2-0 start, falling at Northwestern, at Baylor and at home to Texas Tech. The Buffaloes are rested after an open week. Julian Lewis has thrown for 733 yards with six touchdowns and two interceptions, and Joseph Williams has five touchdown catches. Lamont Lester Jr. has four sacks. Deion Sanders is in his fourth season, and Brennan Marion runs the Go-Go offense. Colorado's offense ranks 95th in ESPN's index; its defense ranks 33rd.

The programs' traditions are strong. Colorado won the 1990 national title, and Rashaan Salaam (1994) and Travis Hunter (2024) won Heisman Trophies. Utah won Pac-12 titles in 2021 and 2022.

The weather should be cool and calm, 62 degrees, for the late kickoff at Folsom Field. Utah backup JC Hart is out.

Utah hosts No. 20 Houston next week. Colorado visits No. 18 Oklahoma State.

Utah's top-10 offense and solid defense give it a clear edge. Colorado's rest and home crowd help, but the Utes' balance should win out. Colorado's best chance is to keep Dampier off the field with long drives and to turn a turnover or two into a short field. The Buffaloes have allowed 29 or more points in two of their three losses, so slowing Parker early is the key.

Our call: Utah 32, Colorado 17.

Running back Adam Mohammed, who has 336 rushing yards, is a game-time decision. AJ Tuitele has three sacks, and Isaiah Crosby has 34 tackles. Tosh Lupoi is in his first season as head coach.

Wake Forest, in Jake Dickert's second season, has one of the most efficient passers in the country. Gio Lopez has completed 124 of 184 passes for 1,680 yards, with 13 touchdowns and one interception. Carlos Hernandez has 49 catches for 720 yards. Langston Hardy has 4.5 sacks, and Vincent Firenze has 44 tackles. ESPN's Football Power Index ranks Wake's offense 20th in efficiency, against a Cal defense ranked 85th. Wake's defense ranks 35th.

The only previous meeting was a 46-36 Cal win at Wake Forest on Nov. 8, 2024.

Cal's history includes national titles claimed for 1920 through 1923 and 1937, and Jeff Tedford's modern revival. Wake Forest won ACC titles in 1970 and 2006, and Dave Clawson spent a decade building the program.

Wake Forest gets an open week before hosting Virginia on Oct. 31. Cal visits No. 24 SMU.

Our score assumes Sagapolutele plays, since he is listed probable. With him, we see Wake Forest 33, California 21. If Brousseau starts again, it would be Wake Forest 34, California 19.

Wake's efficient offense against a struggling Cal defense is the difference.

Our call: Wake Forest 33, California 21.

fanatic_story.body:

Fresno State (4-2, 1-1 Pac-12) visits San Diego State (2-4, 1-1) at 10:30 p.m. ET on CBS Sports Network at Snapdragon Stadium. San Diego State leads the overall series 32-27-4, and Fresno State leads the trophy series 7-6. Last October, the Aztecs won 23-0.

Fresno State's Jayden Mandal has been one of the most careful passers in the country. He has completed 110 of 170 passes for 1,252 yards, with eight touchdowns and one interception, and hasn't thrown an interception in 155 attempts. Josiah Freeman has 396 receiving yards. K'vion Thunderbird leads the defense with 52 tackles, and Dylan Hampsten has three sacks. Matt Entz is in his second season. The Bulldogs won four straight, including 26-6 at Washington State, before last week's 38-31 loss to No. 23 Boise State.

San Diego State has struggled on offense. Jayden Denegal remains the starter and has completed 76 of 141 passes for 787 yards, with six touchdowns and five interceptions. Backup Stone Saunders is questionable. Javion Kinnard has 355 rushing yards, and Sione Hala leads the defense with 61 tackles. Sean Lewis is in his third season, running a veer-and-shoot offense, a passing system where receivers choose routes after the snap. The Aztecs lost 66-14 at Oregon State last week.

ESPN's Football Power Index ranks San Diego State's offense 130th in efficiency, against a Fresno State defense ranked 70th. Fresno State's offense ranks 70th, against an Aztecs defense ranked 74th.

Both programs have proud histories. Pat Hill made Fresno State a giant-killer in the 2000s, and the Bulldogs won Mountain West titles in 2012, 2013, 2018 and 2022. San Diego State won Mountain West titles in 2012, 2015 and 2016.

It should be a warm night, 79 degrees with light wind.

Fresno State hosts Oregon State on Oct. 31. San Diego State visits Colorado State.

Fresno State's balance and Mandal's ball security give it the edge. San Diego State's home field and rivalry energy add a little uncertainty. The Aztecs' best path is to run Kinnard, shorten the game and take advantage of any Fresno State mistakes.

Our call: Fresno State 27, San Diego State 18.

games.story_text:
A long trip to Honolulu awaits New Mexico (4-1, 1-0 Mountain West). Hawai'i (1-5, 0-3) hosts at 10:30 on FS1.

New Mexico insider Paloma Begaye-Ortiz pilots hot-air balloons and says the Lobos are floating high after two weeks of rest. Toa Fa'avae averages over 17 yards a completion, and Scottre Humphrey has six rushing touchdowns. ESPN ranks the Lobo defense seventh in the country. Hawai'i insider Kainoa Akana-Baird loves time-zone math. He's believing in Micah Alejado, who has 1,613 passing yards. Kainoa Carvalho is his top receiver.

New Mexico starting quarterback Jack Layne is out for the season, and linebacker Jaxton Eck is out with a shoulder injury. Hawai'i lost 30-12 at Arizona State. DeVon Rice leads Hawai'i's ground game. Gusts in the low 30s in Honolulu could affect passing, which suits a Lobo team that can run and defend.

Our call: New Mexico 29, Hawai'i 12.
games.why_this_score: New Mexico's elite defense faces a Hawai'i offense that has struggled, and the Lobos are rested. The travel and Hawai'i's home field help keep it within reach. Wind could limit both passing games.
games.betting_text: With New Mexico favored by 14.5 and the total set at 44.5 points, we predict New Mexico 29, Hawai'i 12. New Mexico wins by 17, more than the 14.5-point spread, so New Mexico covers. Our projected total of 41 points is under the 44.5, so we expect the game to go under.
games.total_reason_public: The posted total has dropped from 48.5 to 44.5 since opening, and the forecast calls for wind gusts around 32 mph. We project 41 total points, under the posted 44.5.

fanatic_story.headline: New Mexico's Top-10 Defense Takes On the Wind in Honolulu
fanatic_story.dek: The rested Lobos, 4-1 in Jason Eck's second season, visit a Hawai'i team that has lost four of five, with gusts near 32 mph expected
fanatic_story.body:
HONOLULU — New Mexico has a defense ranked among the nation's best and two weeks of rest. Hawai'i has home field and, possibly, the wind.

New Mexico (4-1, 1-0 Mountain West) visits Hawai'i (1-5, 0-3) at 10:30 p.m. ET on FS1 at the Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex. Hawai'i leads the series 17-11 and won the last meeting 38-30 in Honolulu on Nov. 30, 2024.

ESPN's Football Power Index ranks New Mexico's defense seventh in the country in efficiency. It faces a Hawai'i offense ranked 109th. Brett Karhu has four sacks, and Mercury Swaim leads the team with 25 tackles. The Lobos' only loss was 14-6 at Oklahoma, and they beat UTEP 61-7 on Oct. 3 before an open week.

Quarterback Toa Fa'avae has completed 36 of 63 passes for 639 yards, averaging more than 17 yards per completion, with five touchdowns and one interception. Scottre Humphrey has six rushing touchdowns, and Bailen George has three touchdown catches. Jack Layne has been out since before the season, and Jaxton Eck is out. Jason Eck is in his second season.

Hawai'i has lost four of five, most recently 30-12 at Arizona State. Micah Alejado has completed 157 of 265 passes for 1,613 yards, with five touchdowns and four interceptions. Kainoa Carvalho has 29 catches, and Kona Moore leads the defense with 46 tackles. Timmy Chang is in his fifth season. Anthony Arceneaux runs the run-and-shoot, a passing system where receivers adjust their routes after the snap. Hawai'i's defense ranks 130th, against a New Mexico offense ranked 51st.

The weather may matter most. It should be 83 degrees with gusts near 32 mph and a slight chance of rain, which could limit both passing games. That would seem to suit New Mexico's ground game and defense more than Hawai'i's pass-first offense.

Hawai'i's history includes Dick Tomey, who built the program, and June Jones, who led it to the 2007 WAC title. New Mexico had a long run under Rocky Long and won WAC titles in 1962, 1963 and 1964.

New Mexico hosts North Dakota State next week. Hawai'i visits Northern Illinois.

New Mexico's elite defense and rest give it the edge. The travel and Hawai'i's home crowd help keep the game within reach.

Our call: New Mexico 29, Hawai'i 12.

Kwazi Gilmer has six touchdown catches. That 20-17 Indiana loss stung. Autzen is loud, but nothing beats the sellout streak.

games.story_text:
Late-night Autzen Stadium is one of college football's great environments, and Oregon (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) needs it. Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) visits at 11 p.m. on Fox.

Oregon insider Phoenix "Nix" Wyatt-Aldana reviews uniforms before analyzing football. She gives the Ducks a 10 out of 10 for style, but admits the quarterback picture is complicated. Dante Moore is out with a concussion for a second straight game, so senior Brock Thomas starts. Thomas went 11 of 15 for 156 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter against UCLA. Leading receiver Evan Stewart is doubtful. Nebraska insider Darla Rasmussen brings up the sellout streak every segment. She loves Anthony Colandrea's 13 touchdowns and Kwazi Gilmer's six touchdown catches.

Nebraska lost 20-17 to Indiana last week, and Oregon fell 17-15 to UCLA. Both teams want to get back on track. Mild weather should allow both offenses to play their style.

Our call: Oregon 28, Nebraska 23.
games.why_this_score: Oregon's defense and home crowd give it the edge, even with a backup quarterback. Nebraska's offense is good enough to keep it close. The Ducks' quarterback situation adds uncertainty.
games.betting_text: With Oregon favored by 7 and the total set at 51.5 points, we predict Nebraska 23, Oregon 28. Oregon wins by 5, but Nebraska stays inside the 7-point spread and covers. Our projected total of 51 points is under the 51.5, so we expect the game to go under.

fanatic_story.headline: Oregon Turns to Brock Thomas Against Nebraska
fanatic_story.dek: With Dante Moore out again, the senior makes his first career start as the Ducks try to bounce back from a UCLA loss against a 5-1 Husker team
fanatic_story.body:
EUGENE, Ore. — Oregon lost a 17-15 heartbreaker to UCLA and is down to its next quarterback. Nebraska wants to bounce back from a close loss.

Nebraska (5-1, 2-1 Big Ten) visits Oregon (3-2, 1-1) at 11 p.m. ET on Fox at Autzen Stadium. Nebraska leads the series 6-2. This is the ninth meeting and the first as Big Ten opponents.

Oregon quarterback Dante Moore is out with a concussion for a second straight game. Senior Brock Thomas will make his first career start, chosen over transfer Dylan Raiola. Thomas went 11 of 15 for 156 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter of last week's 17-15 loss to UCLA. Moore has completed 69 of 99 passes for 926 yards and nine touchdowns. Receiver Evan Stewart, who has 352 yards and four touchdowns, is doubtful. Jordon Davison has six rushing touchdowns, Matayo Uiagalelei has five sacks, and Koi Perich has 34 tackles. Dan Lanning is in his fifth season.

Nebraska's Anthony Colandrea has completed 119 of 186 passes for 1,406 yards, with 13 touchdowns and three interceptions. Kwazi Gilmer has six touchdown catches, and Jamal Rule has five rushing touchdowns. Owen Chambliss leads the defense with 31 tackles. Matt Rhule is in his fourth season. The Huskers won five straight before a 20-17 loss to No. 5 Indiana last week.

ESPN's Football Power Index rates this as a strong matchup on both sides. Nebraska's offense ranks 22nd, against an Oregon defense ranked 11th. Oregon's offense ranks 55th, against a Nebraska defense ranked 21st.

Nebraska won five national titles, from Bob Devaney's 1970 champions through 1997, and Johnny Rodgers, Mike Rozier and Eric Crouch won Heisman Trophies. Oregon won the 2024 Big Ten title, and Marcus Mariota won the Heisman in 2014.

It should be a cool, dry night in Eugene, 58 degrees with light wind.

Nebraska has an open week before hosting Washington on Oct. 31. Oregon visits Illinois.

Our score assumes Thomas starts, because Moore is out for a second straight game. With Thomas, we see Oregon 28, Nebraska 23. If Moore were able to play, it would be Oregon 30, Nebraska 21.

Oregon's defense and home crowd give it the edge, even with a backup quarterback. Nebraska's offense is good enough to keep it close.

Our call: Oregon 28, Nebraska 23.
